items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Mastercard and BVNK launched the Global Money Platform, a modular infrastructure layer letting businesses embed multi-currency accounts holding fiat and stablecoins side by side.
- It ties into Mastercard Move for local-currency payouts and lets users spend stablecoin balances across Mastercard’s merchant network, with Nuvei and Marqeta among first integrators.
- Mastercard framed it for a “multi-money” future, with planned support for agentic commerce and tokenized deposits.
Mastercard is folding stablecoins into its sprawling payments empire, launching a platform that lets businesses hold, move, and spend traditional currencies and digital dollars side by side through a single connection.
Unveiled Thursday, the Mastercard Global Money Platform pairs the payments giant’s global network with the stablecoin infrastructure of BVNK, the crypto firm Mastercard acquired in August.
Mastercard struck the deal to buy BVNK for roughly $1.8 billion, and the new platform marks the first major integration of the two companies’ capabilities since that acquisition closed.
At the center of the platform is what Mastercard calls a global money account, a multi-currency account where fiat and stablecoins can sit together, with conversion between them handled through a single API.
Banks, fintechs and enterprises can embed those accounts into their own branded products, along with real-time conversion, stablecoin-linked cards and local bank payouts, or use the platform to run their own treasury and settlement. The pitch is a modular toolkit spanning sending, receiving, converting, storing, spending and earning, letting customers start with the pieces they need and bolt on more over time.
Mastercard framed the offering as plumbing for a “multi-money” world. The platform ties into Mastercard Move, the company’s money-transfer network, letting users tap stablecoin balances to send local-currency payments into recipients’ bank accounts, with coverage expected to reach more than 40 currencies across 200-plus countries in 2027. Customers will also be able to spend stablecoin balances across Mastercard’s merchant-acceptance network, with card issuing available in more than 130 countries.
Payments firm Nuvei and card-issuing platform Marqeta are among the first to integrate the platform, alongside Ontop, Beem, and Almond FinTech.
Raj Dhamodharan, Mastercard’s executive vice president for blockchain and digital assets, said the company believes “the future of commerce will be built on interoperability across multiple forms of money,” calling the launch a step toward enabling “the next generation of programmable and agentic commerce.”
That nod to agentic commerce, where AI agents transact on their own, signals where Mastercard sees the puck heading.
The company has already moved to enable AI-agent payments alongside crypto heavyweights like Coinbase and Ripple, and secured a New York BitLicense covering stablecoins and tokenized deposits. Mastercard said Global Money Platform will add support for agentic commerce and tokenized deposits down the line.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments
The launch of Global Money Platform marks Mastercard’s first major integration with BVNK since its August acquisition, with Nuvei and Marqeta among the first companies to adopt the platform.
Mastercard is expanding its role in stablecoin payments with a new platform that lets businesses integrate digital currencies into traditional banking and card services, a move that could make it easier for companies to offer stablecoin payments without building their own infrastructure.
The service, dubbed Global Money Platform, is Mastercard’s first major integration with BVNK since it acquired the stablecoin infrastructure company in August, the payments giant announced Thursday.
According to Mastercard, businesses can use the platform to hold and convert fiat currencies and stablecoins, offer stablecoin-linked cards and make payments directly from stablecoin balances into recipients’ local bank accounts.
The service connects to Mastercard Move, the company’s global money transfer network, which can route payments to more than 17 billion destinations, including bank accounts and cards. It also connects stablecoin balances to Mastercard’s merchant network, allowing customers to spend them with payment cards. Nuvei, Marqeta and several other fintech companies are among the first integration partners.
The launch extends Mastercard’s role beyond processing payments to providing infrastructure that financial companies can use to offer stablecoin services under their own brands. It also puts Mastercard in closer competition with Visa, which launched a platform in July that lets financial institutions hold, mint, and transfer stablecoins.
It comes as research from Standard Chartered points to growing stablecoin transaction activity, even as the circulating supplies of major tokens such as USDt and USDC have remained relatively flat this year.
Related: US accounting overhaul could make stablecoins more attractive to corporations: Tempo
items.title: Mastercard brings stablecoin balances into traditional banking and card payments

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Crypto liquidations reached $948.22 million in 24 hours across 177,440 traders, with long positions accounting for 90.6%, per CoinGlass.
- Bitcoin fell 2.6% and broke support after hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI data revived bets on another Fed rate hike.
- Bitcoin now trades roughly 2% below the average cost of U.S. spot ETF holders near $82,300, putting those buyers back underwater.
Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Thursday for the first time in over a month, extending Wednesday’s inflation-driven slide and wiping out nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets. It's currently trading just about $82,000 after several hours of increased volatility.
Ethereum and XRP dropped close to 5%, Zcash sank almost 10%, and only five coins in the top 100 managed gains above 1%. Pick any coin in the top 100 and it's likely in the red today.
Across the market, 177,440 traders were liquidated in 24 hours for a total of $948.22 million, per CoinGlass, with longs accounting for $858.96 million, or 90.6%. Ethereum led with $282.03 million, with Bitcoin just behind at a little over $200 million.
This was the third-heaviest day for long liquidations in the last 90 days, behind October 8 and August 22. The largest single order liquidated yesterday was a $12.03 million Bitcoin long on Binance, force-closed at $80,208.96.
A liquidation happens when a trader borrows to bet on a price move and the market goes the other way. Once losses eat through the collateral, the exchange sells the position automatically, and that forced selling drags prices lower and trips the next batch of leveraged longs.
The trigger was Wednesday’s inflation report, which showed consumer prices up 3.7% year over year in September against a 3.6% forecast, with core inflation at 2.6% against 2.5%. Thursday’s Producer Price Index, which tracks business input costs, rose 6.3% annually versus a 5.5% forecast.
Much of that inflation comes from oil, with Brent crude near $104 a barrel, about 70% above a year ago amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. That feeds into fuel, shipping, and almost everything else that needs to be transported to reach consumers.
Hot inflation pushes the Federal Reserve toward higher interest rates, which lifts Treasury yields, the return investors earn for lending to the U.S. government. A bond paying around 5% with almost no risk makes Bitcoin a harder sell, while higher rates make borrowing pricier and strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money leveraged crypto traders run on.
Iliya Kalchev, analyst at Nexo, reads the selloff as a broad exit from risk more than a Fed story, with stocks and copper falling, gold rising and South Korea’s Kospi down about 8%.
“Bitcoin has slipped to the bottom of the $81,000 to $87,000 range it has held since late September, and Glassnode flags $80,000 as the level to watch,” Kalchev told Decrypt. “It is also now roughly 2% below the average cost of U.S. spot ETF holders, near $82,300, after closing above that line on 21 of the 24 days since September 21. That puts ETF buyers back underwater, and reclaiming it is the first test of any rebound,”
On the daily chart, Bitcoin broke below $81,603, the strongest upper support from its August-to-October rally from $62,763 to $87,422, where uptrend pullbacks often stall. The drop reached $79,711 before buyers pulled the price back near $80,925, off a rising trend band near $80,286.
The Relative Strength Index, a 0-to-100 momentum gauge where 50 splits bulls from bears, fell to about 44, while the golden cross still keeps the longer-term uptrend intact.
A daily close back above $81,603 would reopen the path to $84,245 and the $87,422 swing high. Losing $80,286 would expose $78,002 as the next support, and then $75,092.
Kalchev sees early signs the selling is not deepening, including cooling profit-taking, but said a recovery needs more than a bounce.
“Three things need to line up for Bitcoin to push through. ETF flows have to turn consistently positive, after $681 million of outflows last week and a single $177 million inflow day. Selling by long-term holders has to ease,” Kalchev explained.
For Kalchev, a bullish market would require that leverage happens with a sustained buying instead of just a bounce. He added that a “Fed path that stops at one 25 basis point hike would take some pressure off the backdrop.”
The Fed announces its rate decision on October 28, followed by core PCE inflation data the next day and October payrolls on November 6.

items.author: Cointelegraph by William Suberg
items.content:
Bitcoin slips under $80K after US PPI gains most in four years
BTC buyers attempted to defend $80,000 support after September US producer inflation overshot expectations by 100 basis points for the largest monthly gain since March 2022
Bitcoin (BTC) dipped below $80,000 on Thursday as US Producer Price Index (PPI) data significantly beat expectations.
Key points:
- Bitcoin briefly traded below $80,000 on the back of a 100-basis-point overshoot in US PPI inflation data.
- September PPI measured 6.3% against market expectations of 5.3%, the biggest monthly jump since March 2022.
- BTC price analysis saw the potential for a “volatile retest” of trend lines around $78,000 next.
Biggest PPI increase since March 2022 adds to Bitcoin tailwinds
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD slipping to its lowest levels since Sept. 18, declining as much as 1.8% on the day, before rebounding to around $81,000.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
September PPI came in at 6.3%, a full 100 basis points above its anticipated level, while core PPI rose to 5% versus an expected 4.4%, per data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).
“The September increase is the largest advance since rising 1.7% in March 2022. On an unadjusted basis, the index for final demand climbed 6.3% for the 12 months ended in September, the largest 12-month increase since moving up 6.4% in December 2022,” an official news release confirmed.
US PPI one-month % change. Source: BLS
The numbers come a day after the Consumer Price Index (CPI) also overshot estimates, causing crypto and risk assets to fall. Risk assets were already under pressure from a tech sell-off centered in South Korea, where the KOSPI Composite Index fell 7.5% on Thursday.
Economist Mohamed El-Erian described PPI as “even more striking” than the CPI result. El-Erian and others noted that US bond yields were not rising on the back of higher inflation numbers. The US 10-year bond yield was down almost 3% at the time of writing, at its lowest levels since Sept. 23.
US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Robin Brooks, former chief FX strategist at Goldman Sachs, repeated earlier findings which suggested that yields had “decoupled” from US macro data as market priorities switched to the government’s handling of the federal budget deficit.
Brooks compared the 30-day correlation between upside data surprises and daily moves in the 10-year yield, and revealed that it had dropped from near 0.6 earlier in 2026 to just below zero as of the end of August.
“That indicates that yields have decoupled from data and the obvious explanation for this is that markets are more focused on the trajectory of the deficit, so they’re pushing up longer-term yields regardless of what data surprises are doing,” he summarized in a blog post last month.
Analysis eyes “early-stage bull market” support retest
BTC price action meanwhile brought two support trend lines back into focus: the 21-week and 50-week exponential moving averages (EMA) at $76,144 and $78.459, respectively.
Related: CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
Trader and analyst Rekt Capital noted that BTC/USD could still retest both and preserve its overall bullish trend.
“Deviating below them on a volatile retest to find a pullback bottom has historically happened in early-stage Bull Markets. These deviations however would occur after a bullish crossovers of these two EMAs, whereas Bitcoin is still pre-crossover,” Rekt Capital said in an X post.
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
Bitcoin remained below the area between $82,500 and $82,800, a key support zone of interest in recent weeks.
Analyst Aksel Kibar said that Bitcoin’s latest weekly close around $83,700 lacked strength as a breakout.
“A weekly close inside the range can resume wide consolidation between 60K-82.8K 75K can be utilized as the pattern (rectangle bottom reversal) negation level,” he said.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Aksel Kibar on X.com

[EvanAnderson]: The Computer History Museum collected an oral history[0] of John Backus[1] and there's some discussion about what computing was like when Fortran was created. I really enjoy CHM's oral histories. I'm slowly working my way thru all of them and there are some real gems in there (Ken Thompson, Dennis Ritchie, Margaret Hamilton, Gordon Moore, Fred Brooks, John Warnock, etc). [0]  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dDsWTyLEgbk  [1]  https://en.wikipedia.org&#x2...

[obviouslynotme]: I used to work on software that still uses Fortran from the 50's and is still in maintenance and use today. IIRC, it had ~700kloc of Fortran. It may be the oldest and largest Fortran codebase still in use. My first project there was removing all of the Hollerith from the code. Since Fortran predated strings, you had to manipulate them as integers. When you tied that to the original Fortran dynamic memory system, Dynosour, which used equivalenced arrays as pointers, it was a disaster. It ...

[whartung]: FORTRAN was a very important language for me. Growing up on early micros, with BASIC, my father had Fortran for the TRS-80. I took a stab at learning it, but the documentation was reference for calling the compiler, not so much learning the language. And when I found a FORTRAN book, it was quite dated and talking about things like tapes and punches and what not. So, that effort stalled. But, my first quarter in college, I took a FORTRAN (77) class. FORTRAN taught on the schools CDC Cyber main...

[dranudin]: I wrote Fortran for my first job as a software developer in 2018 for simulation solvers. Still like the language! Modern fortran is very very fast and much nicer to use than C for linear algebra. So in my opinion for numerical calculations it remains the best language, even today.
Happy Birthday!

[ggm]: Used to man the free help desk for programming problems at the uni computing centre I worked at. "Have you got a current listing of the program" got rid of most of them. Saddest case was a PhD student in chemical engineering near the end of his thesis work struggling to get reproducible results. After half an hour of debug I realised he was using un-initialised Fortran array state for his data. I suspect his discovery went up in smoke.

items.content:
Crypto for Advisors: Wall Street is done waiting on Congress for crypto rules
You’re reading Crypto for Advisors, CoinDesk’s weekly newsletter that unpacks digital assets for financial advisors. Subscribe here to get it every Thursday.
Happy Thursday, advisors!
In today’s newsletter, Eric Soufer of Tusk Strategies looks at what financial firms are building while Congress stalls on a crypto framework.
Then, in “Ask an Expert,” Diego Grassano explains what advisors should check before trusting a tokenized platform.
Happy reading.
While Congress stalls, Wall Street sets its own crypto rule
Without a federal framework, financial firms are standardizing compliance and infrastructure on their own.
When the Senate failed to advance the CLARITY Act on Sept. 15, the U.S. was once again left without a comprehensive federal framework for digital assets, and regulators moved to fill part of the gap. Two days later, the SEC issued an “innovation exemption” allowing certain venues to trade tokenized U.S.-listed stocks onchain.
But an exemption is not a statute, and it can be narrowed or withdrawn as easily as it was granted. That leaves financial firms with a practical question: What do you build while you wait? For advisors, the answer matters more than who won or lost in Washington.
That question ran through a Crain’s New York Business event last week, whether the topic was tokenization, compliance or cybersecurity. The people closest to the work aren’t waiting for Congress. They’re building for the world as it is.
Adam Schumann, vice president of legal at OKX, laid out the legal problem. U.S. firms answer to federal statutes, federal agencies, state laws and state regulators, and none of them move at the same speed. “You want general consistency, but you’re not going to reach uniformity,” he said. Firms work out the rest state by state and country by country, while agencies patch the most immediate gaps.
That patchwork has a cost. Aravind Raju, CFO of Uphold, said compliance is now one of the company’s largest departments because it builds tailored solutions for each state’s requirements. As rules become clearer and more aligned, he expects those resources can be redirected. For advisors, the takeaway is that compliance is a real cost of doing business on these platforms, and the firms that manage it well will have an edge.
You might expect that duplication to push the industry toward shared infrastructure. Instead, many institutions launched private, closed networks this year for tokenized assets, stablecoins and securities ledgers, and those networks can’t easily talk to one another. Lewis Tuff, CEO of Twilight, which builds clearing and settlement technology, said the result is that every firm ends up rebuilding the same connections.
Risk is moving in the opposite direction, toward separation. Early crypto firms bundled trading, custody and clearing under one roof. Today, traditional custodians hold digital assets, and the venues that execute trades are increasingly separate from the ones that safeguard them. That means no single entity has to hold every key function or become a single point of failure. Compliance and security are shifting too, from annual attestations and periodic reviews to checks that run continuously, with every transaction.
None of this required Congress, and that’s the point. Without a comprehensive framework, the industry is converging on practices any future law would find hard to ignore: verified counterparties, clear lines between trading and custody, and compliance that never stops running.
Whether these practices become a bridge to legislation or a substitute for it is still an open question, but the direction is clear. Raju offered one prediction. Within three years, he said, “we’ll probably stop using the word ‘crypto’ as tokenized Treasuries and money funds become routine.”
If he’s right, the infrastructure being built now, without a statute to guide it, will matter well beyond this cycle.
- Eric Soufer, partner and head of advanced tech, Tusk Strategies
Ask an Expert
Q. Regulatory Vulnerability: How risky is it for institutions to pour capital into infrastructure built on temporary SEC exemptions and state-level workarounds?
The main risk is committing long-term capital to infrastructure that may only have temporary permission to operate. Exemptions can help institutions get started, but they need a credible plan if those permissions change or expire. I’d want clear ownership rights, segregated custody and a tested exit route that allows investors to recover their assets.
Q. Solving Fragmentation: How can institutions bridge siloed, private blockchains without compromising security or regulatory isolation?
Institutions need to connect networks without losing control over ownership, compliance or privacy. Bridges are improving but still carry real security and operational risks. While regulatory standards remain fragmented, I’d keep the legally recognized ownership record on the original chain and allow backed, redeemable representations to circulate elsewhere, with eligibility and transfer restrictions enforced on both networks.
Q. Actionable Advisor Takeaways: What criteria should financial advisors use to vet tokenized platforms when federal investor protections are still in limbo?
I would start with two questions: What does my client actually own, and how do they get their money back? Then check who holds the assets, who independently verifies the numbers and what happens if the platform fails. Look closely at fees, conflicts and withdrawal restrictions. If an advisor cannot clearly explain the ownership structure, the risks and the recovery process to a client, the due diligence is not finished.
- Diego Grassano, commercial director, Shyft; chief product officer, Lumia

items.content:
In brief
- Ethereum, XRP, and Solana have all dropped in value on the day, with "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin.
- Experts point to Wednesday's consumer price index coming in at 3.7% and expectations of an October interest rate hike as major macro pressures.
- The slide is also a natural hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.
Altcoins have taken a hit over the past 24 hours, with major tokens seeing "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin. Experts say that this has largely been prompted by macro pressures pushing prices down.
With the market cap of all cryptocurrencies dropping by 2.5% to $2.8 trillion, Ethereum dropped by 5.5% to a $289 billion market cap over the past 24 hours, XRP fell by 5.1% to $82.4 billion, and Solana slipped by 3.8% to $60.6 billion. Meanwhile, industry leader Bitcoin has slipped by 3.1% on the day and 2.6% on the week, sitting at a market cap of $1.6 trillion.
It comes after the consumer price index rose 3.7% in the year to September, as Decrypt reported on Wednesday, with Myriad predictors pointing to a 28% chance of an October interest rate hike (Disclaimer: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company Dastan).
Nick Forster, founder of options trading exchange Derive.xyz, said in a note shared with Decrypt that this shifted traders into "protection mode" as "hedging activity" on the platform doubled, and whales pulled back on optimistic bets made in spring.
"This immediate pull-back from long-term upside bets alongside aggressive short-term hedging shows a dramatic regime shift," he said, "with institutional participants rapidly reassessing their macro risk exposure as the path for interest rates turns murky again."
When markets react like this, Luke Nolan, senior research associate at CoinShares, says that altcoins are impacted the most.
"[It] seems to be high beta assets just got hit harder, similar to in equities as well, where the high flyers have seen outsized drawdowns in recent sessions," Nolan told Decrypt. "Alts are typically more sensitive to financial conditions, and tightening affects the premise of liquidity expanding."
Nolan also highlighted the U.S. dollar hitting a near 18-month high as a downward pressure on the entire crypto market. He said that over a medium-term horizon, crypto tends to have an inverse correlation to the US Dollar Index, or DXY. This is partly due to crypto being priced in dollars, Nolan explained, but also because a rising dollar causes a tightening in liquidity and a fall in risk appetite.
Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt that the slide is also a hangover from altcoins’ “strength and momentum” over recent months.
Since the start of October, futures open interest in altcoins (excluding Ethereum) has fallen by $8 billion, Shannon said. To him, that shows traders have “taken chips off the table,” which is a natural reaction after such a strong run.
That pattern is playing out with Ethereum, he added. ETH outperformed Bitcoin for three consecutive months, the first time it’s managed that since March 2021, and investors have been cashing in since. Ethereum ETFs saw 11 straight trading days of net outflows totalling $782.8 million, he said, before a brief inflow on Tuesday. Money has been heading back out since, per CoinGlass data, with $129.5 million in net outflows.
"This price action is more of a consolidation period for altcoins that have already done well," Shannon told Decrypt. "Altcoins generally tend to exhibit high correlations with BTC in tough times and lower correlations, especially with idiosyncratic catalysts, in better market environments. Hence, for the near term, it is possible that these altcoins trade in lockstep with BTC, albeit more sensitively."
For prices to recover, Nolan says he wants to see expectations of an interest rate hike in October to fall. Right now, he struggles to call a bottom for altcoins as he sees valid arguments for movements in either direction.
"I could see a situation where Bitcoin loses its support and altcoins likely bleed further," Nolan told Decrypt. "The opposite could also be true: this could be just a short-term correction, and we could be back into decent market conditions soon, which if Bitcoin was to push back decently above 80k, I could very well see an outsized up move for altcoins."

items.author: Cointelegraph by Helen Partz
items.content:
Russia to ban direct peer-to-peer crypto trades starting July 2027
Russia plans to ban direct P2P crypto trades from July 1, 2027, while separate rules already prohibit transfers from digital accounts to self-custody wallets.
Russia will ban direct peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency transactions between individuals starting next year, requiring individuals to use authorized intermediaries for such trades.
The restriction will end individuals’ ability to exchange crypto assets directly without intermediaries, the Bank of Russia, the country’s central bank, explained in guidance updated Monday. The regulator confirmed that such transactions will remain permitted only until July 1, 2027.
The regulator also clarified that individuals are not allowed to transfer crypto assets from their digital accounts to their own non-custodial, or self-custodial, wallets.
The move comes as Russia expands its regulated crypto market. On Monday, the Bank of Russia authorized Sberbank, the country’s largest bank, to offer crypto exchange services after earlier approving it as a digital asset custodian.
The approval follows Russia’s new crypto rules, which came into force on Sept. 1 and brought exchange operators and custodians under central bank oversight. The country also continues to prohibit cryptocurrency payments for goods and services.
Industry executives have previously told Cointelegraph that restrictions on P2P crypto trading and noncustodial wallets may be difficult to enforce. Jan3 CEO Samson Mow said P2P trading is more resilient to regulatory crackdowns than centralized platforms, while SatoshiLabs executive Stepan Uherik said wallet app bans would leave hardware and desktop wallets unaffected.
Related: Russia clears first crypto exchanges, custodians under new law

items.content:
Nasdaq-listed Tron sets up $200M ATM share offering to fuel TRX acquisitions
The Nasdaq-listed treasury company holds about $237 million in TRX tokens and plans to raise additional capital to fund its purchases, alongside its daily accumulation.
Nasdaq-listed Tron (TRON) has filed for a new at-the-market (ATM) share offering allowing it to sell up to $200 million of common stock that will fund an even-larger Tron (TRX) treasury.
The deal allows Tron to periodically sell shares of its common stock at $0.0001 par value through Clear Street, which acts as an agent and retains a commission of up to 3% of gross proceeds, according to a Wednesday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
The company’s existing TRX accumulation program, announced in February, called for the purchase of approximately $50,000 worth of TRX per day for 360 consecutive days. Tron’s treasury holds 718.9 million TRX tokens, currently worth about $237 million, after the company’s latest acquisition of 149,369 TRX at an average price of $0.3347 on Thursday.
Tron SEC filing on a $200 million ATM program with Clear Street LLC. Source: sec.gov
The company’s shares opened 4.7% lower on Thursday, poised to extend their roughlly 67% 12-month decline, according to Yahoo Finance.
Related: XRP treasury Evernorth’s shares rise 5% at Nasdaq opening print
items.title: Nasdaq-listed Tron sets up $200M ATM share offering to fuel TRX acquisitions

Bitwise CIO：无论AI繁荣还是泡沫破裂，比特币长期都可能受益

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，Bitwise 首席投资官 Matt Hougan 在致客户报告中表示，无论 AI 推动经济繁荣、投资泡沫破裂，还是经济仅温和增长，比特币长期都可能受益。在 AI 泡沫破裂并引发类似 2008 年衰退的情景下，鉴于 AI 的地缘政治重要性，他认为政府随后实施救助的概率「接近 100%」。比特币可能先遭抛售，再随货币供应量激增而大幅上涨。

若 AI 大幅提升生产力及 GDP、降低软件和法律服务等成本，Hougan 预计，比特币等仍然稀缺的资产将升值。若经济维持 3% 增长、4% 利率并接近软着陆，ETF 资金流入、投顾采用，以及企业和主权资产负债表配置仍可支撑比特币。

他提醒，比特币不会直线上涨，部分情景可能先经历困难阶段。量子计算威胁、政府协同打压或西方政府重新实施财政紧缩，也可能使其判断失效；他认为这些情况不太可能发生，但并非不可能。

纳斯达克拟设500万美元市值退市门槛，引发美国本土小企业反对

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据彭博社报道，纳斯达克拟对市值低于 500 万美元达 30 天的上市公司立即停牌，随后面临退市，以打击微盘股「拉高出货」等操纵行为。该提案遭美国本土小企业反对，监管机构上月已暂缓推进，并进一步征求公众意见。

彭博数据显示，目前超过 190 家纳斯达克上市公司市值不超过 500 万美元，其中约三分之一位于亚洲，近半位于美国。反对企业认为，交易清淡导致的自然价格波动不等于市场操纵，提案可能吓退融资、误伤正常经营的企业。与现有低股价退市规则提供的 180 天整改期不同，新提案没有较长宽限期。

纳斯达克则表示，市场赋予极低估值的证券更易出现波动，对公平有序交易构成持续挑战。NYSE American 今年 3 月也提出类似 500 万美元门槛，SEC 同样推迟了最终表决。

items.content:
In brief
- Ledger has announced Atom, a touchscreen Android device that incorporates a Secure Element running Ledger OS.
- Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner, with its Seeker app and Solana dApp Store preinstalled on Ledger's new Atom device.
- The launch comes as Ledger investigates hidden implants found in hardware wallets sold through a reseller in Southeast Asia.
Ledger's new Atom device will ship with Solana's Seeker app preinstalled, the companies announced on stage at Ledger's Op3n conference in Paris on Thursday.
Billed as a "signer" rather than a hardware wallet, the Atom is an Android-powered touchscreen device equipped with a data-only eSIM and Ledger's Secure Element, enabling users to send and receive encrypted messages with other Atom users as well as perform crypto transactions in the manner of its range of wallets. To do so, the device switches into a Ledger OS-powered "Secure Mode" for sensitive operations such as signing transactions and authorising AI agent requests.
The Atom sports a 6.77-inch OLED display, rear camera and 4,000mAh battery, and runs on a Qualcomm Dragonwing chip. It also incorporates a hardware privacy switch that physically cuts power to the camera and microphone.
The device also runs third-party apps, and will come preinstalled with Solana's Seeker app after Solana Mobile named Ledger as its first hardware expansion partner. Seeker combines Solana Mobile's wallet with its Solana dapp Store, which lists more than 1,500 decentralized apps, and will appear on Atom's home screen. Until now, the store was available on Solana Mobile's own Seeker phone.
Your wealth is digital. The device you manage it with should be built for that.
Meet Ledger Atom™: the security of industry leading hardware, the convenience of your everyday apps, plus control over your AI tools, and a rapidly expanding platform of apps, all in one quantum… pic.twitter.com/vHhDNQYipz
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 15, 2026
Ledger Atom runs on the Android Open Source Project, the free, open version of Google's mobile operating system, alongside a Secure Element chip running Ledger OS. Its display and touch controls are physically isolated from Android, according to the release, and approvals in the Seeker app happen in a "Secure Mode" backed by the Secure Element.
"Having the Seeker app on Ledger Atom from day one just makes sense, so Ledger users get access to the Solana ecosystem without giving up any of the security," said Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer.
Solana Mobile began opening its software stack to other Android manufacturers in March. Samsung Wallet also recently added USDC transfers on Solana. Seeker has handled more than $13 billion in transaction volume and 154 million transactions, according to the company, which says it has sold more than 200,000 devices across Seeker and its earlier Saga phone.
Hardware makers that integrate the stack can earn rewards in SKR, the native token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem, which also rewards users and developers, the release said.
Existing Seeker phones will remain fully supported, Solana Mobile said. Reservations for Ledger Atom are open now, though neither company has given a price or shipping date.
Ledger investigates tampered devices
The Ledger Atom will include anti-tampering and tamper-evident features from the packaging to the device itself, according to the press release, including ways to help detect whether the enclosure has been opened, and will only be sold through Ledger's official site.
The announcement of the Atom comes at an awkward time for Ledger, as the firm investigates tampered devices in its reseller network linked to a suspected $87 million wallet drain.
The company this week disclosed that its Donjon security team had found an implant in a hardware wallet sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis that captures recovery phrases during setup and sends them out over LTE. On Tuesday, it asked resellers in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to pull its devices from shelves.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Andrew Fenton
items.content:
Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion
The SEC and the CFTC have issued a raft of pro-crypto rules recently. But will the rules hold up in court, and can they be easily rolled back by the “anti-crypto army”?
In the wake of the failed CLARITY cloture vote in the Senate, the SEC and CFTC immediately moved to issue their own rules for crypto markets.
Two days after the vote, the SEC unveiled a five-year exemption that permits the issuing and trading of stock tokens. OXK has since teamed up with ICE to launch trading in 63 NYSE-listed stocks and Securitize launched 12 Securitize Stocks, including Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft.
The SEC has also issued guidance clarifying that a crypto token doesn’t become a security just because a project is buying back its own tokens, and stated that liquid staking tokens are not securities. It has also proposed new rules for the custody of crypto assets.
The CFTC, meanwhile, moved to exempt some crypto software providers from registration requirements. It has proposed a new “crypto asset market” registration category and intends to allow registered exchanges to offer leveraged trading.
But the concern among some in the industry is that these rules could be built on shifting sands. TD Cowen has cautioned that agency rules “are the easiest to rescind” — which was demonstrated when Trump-appointed commissioners wiped away all traces of the Gary Gensler era.
A 2024 Supreme Court decision also means agency rules can more easily be overturned by the courts. 
The durability of regulator rulemaking is currently being tested in court, with a community bank group suing the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for exceeding its authority by allowing crypto firms to obtain national trust bank charters.
To discuss the legal issues involved, Magazine spoke with Yuriy Brisov from D&A Partners. This is an edited version of the conversation.
Magazine: SEC Chair Paul Atkins said after the CLARITY vote failed that the agency was releasing rules because Congress didn’t. Are agencies like the SEC supposed to create rules, or are they just supposed to interpret rules that already exist?
Brisov: They are supposed to create rules. They have this power under the Exchange Act of 1934. The SEC was created as a result of the major meltdown in the US markets in the end of the 1920s. From the moment of creation, the SEC had the power to create rules and regulations on how the laws should apply. American legislation works by creating general rules, like a frame, and then it has a watchdog watching over these regulations. 
There was a reason why it was created like this — so that when, say, blockchain tokens came along, the US legislation would be ready to accommodate new technology. That’s what the Commission has been doing for ages now, and it’s obviously within their powers.
Magazine: Can they interpret the rules in the opposite way to an SEC appointed by a previous administration?
Brisov: There should be a reason for that. They can, in theory, do that, but it should be all within the formation of the body of law. Under Gary Gensler, the Commission tried to apply these rules to tokens. It turns out that it failed because there is still vagueness, and many companies left the US market for good.
This is the opening for the new Commission to oversee these rules and say, “You tried, but we can see that it’s not working. So we’ll offer our own rules.” But the power to offer rules is limited. If they offer some regulations that would lay an unbearable economic burden on companies, or something bizarre, there are also laws that allow companies or any damaged party to challenge this regulation in court and say, “We don’t like what the SEC has been doing because it’s damaging the market.”
In 2011, there was a case when the SEC applied new rules on how shareholders vote through a proxy. And the business community said, “it’s bizarre, it’s burdensome, and we don’t like it.” There was a case, Business Roundtable vs SEC, and [business] won.
Magazine: What was the Chevron decision by the Supreme Court and how does its overturning in 2024 impact court cases about rulemaking by agencies like the SEC and CFTC?
Brisov: Chevron was a famous case of 1984. The court basically said that if the law is vague or there are uncertainties and ambiguities in the statute, then we should use the agency’s interpretation as the law. In June 2024, Loper Bright was a new precedent that overruled Chevron. It’s now saying that we don’t have to. Of course, [the SEC is] a strong authority: Who knows securities laws better than the SEC? But the court should use its own brains and apply the Howey case itself.
Magazine: So that makes it more likely that SEC rules could be overturned?
Brisov: In some cases, the courts can come up with a different conclusion.
You cannot just come and say “we don’t like this regulation.” For instance, if you’re a traditional broker-dealer or traditional participant of the investment market in the United States and you say, ‘Look, I’m suffering because of this new regulation’ they should be able to prove that there was not enough research and that it’s burdensome for the business, and it’s not profitable for the US market. If they prove damages and if they prove a lack of research, then the court can overrule this regulation.
From what I can see, Paul Atkins and the SEC have been consulting with many crypto firms, with VCs. They’ve been doing their research, so it’s not something they just came up with within a day.
Related: OKX, NYSE parent file to launch tokenized US stock platform
Magazine: Let’s assume the SEC and CFTC rules survive for the next two years, and businesses invest a lot of money into infrastructure around tokenized stocks based on the new rules. Could a new SEC unilaterally reverse the rules or do they have to take into account the businesses built on top of the old interpretation?
Brisov: They have to take them into account. If there is the potential for the US market to grow and to benefit from this regulation, they won’t be able to just overrule it. There is the same thought process that either an agency or a court goes through. It’s called IRAC: issue, rule, analysis, conclusion. They would have to apply understandable, transparent logic.
They can’t just say we don’t like it. They have to explain. They have to bring up an economic background for it. They have to bring up research, and they have to prove that it’s insufficient. And only then can they come to a different conclusion. 
For the sake of argument, we could say that Paul Atkins hates the Howey test, and he would have been happy just to abandon it — but he can’t do it. In every note, he keeps repeating that the Howey case still works, it’s still a valid regulation in the United States. However, we can interpret it in this case, and this case, differently — and this is our logic. This is what allows us to do that, and he explains it transparently. 
Magazine: The SEC appears to have been working on the innovation exemption for years. But the SEC more recently came up with an FAQ saying that a crypto company buying back its own token does not make a commodity token a security. Could I be secure and comfortable launching a token buyback scheme on the basis of an FAQ by the SEC?
Brisov: If you follow it, and it’s created by the people who know what they’re saying, probably you will be in the clear. But it’s not legislation. An FAQ is just like a manual. It doesn’t have any authority, even for the staff.
Magazine: So the FAQ isn’t saying they changed the rules; it is just saying this is what the rules are?
Brisov: It’s just some extra explanation, like a casebook in the university. They are staff notes. A manual that explains for the staff how they should work and how they should understand this. They rewrite them quite often.
Magazine: They rewrote the FAQ after a week because a16z’s legal counsel said it left a massive loophole.
Brisov: Exactly, and that’s how it should be done. It’s not regulation or legislation, they can change them every week.

⚡️芯片股市值蒸发1万亿美元，投资者逆势涌入半导体ETF抄底

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，随着芯片股市值蒸发 1 万亿美元，ETF 投资者正趁跌势投入数十亿美元，其中一只提供三倍半导体行业每日收益敞口的基金，本周资金流入规模有望创下历史纪录。汇编的数据显示，规模达 720 亿美元的 VanEck 半导体 ETF 过去三个交易日吸引超过 4.3 亿美元资金流入，有望创下 9 月初以来最大单周资金流入规模。部分投资者更加激进，尽管三倍杠杆的 Direxion 每日半导体看涨 3 倍 ETF 本周累计下跌近 21%，仍有约 38 亿美元资金流入。对于这只规模达 190 亿美元的基金而言，这一资金流入规模足以使其创下历史最高单周纪录。

然而，市场背景并不乐观。由于投资者持续担忧人工智能支出和全球竞争加剧，费城半导体指数过去六个交易日累计下跌 12%，市值蒸发约 1 万亿美元。估值过高和利率上升的担忧进一步加剧了该行业的波动。Baird Strategas 首席 ETF 策略师 Todd Sohn 表示：「半导体股的回调走势再次加速，但这仍未能真正抑制投资者利用杠杆逢低买入的需求。」

纽约市审计长呼吁Anthropic暂缓IPO，先应对AI安全及治理风险

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据彭博社报道，纽约市审计长 Mark Levine 周三致信 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei，呼吁公司在充分应对 AI 安全、治理及发展速度相关风险前暂缓 IPO，优先处理该技术带来的前所未有的风险。Levine 负责监督资产规模超过 3250 亿美元的公共养老金。

Levine 认为，特朗普政府与包括 Anthropic 在内的 AI 企业达成的「具有道德约束力」的安全协议仍不足。他敦促 Anthropic 建立相应治理机制，具体披露如何实施适当审计及控制措施、措施覆盖范围和预计时间表，并解释这些措施能否、以及如何回应 Amodei 此前放缓 AI 模型能力发展速度的呼吁。

Anthropic 计划最早于下月上市，募资规模可能达到或超过 SpaceX 此前创纪录的 IPO。公司周三在总部与部分投资者会面，并披露今年第三季度营收为 168 亿美元。Anthropic 未立即回应置评请求。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372073

--- Top Comments ---

[tenacious_tuna]: This is a really enjoyable take, pushing the feeling of what one does on a computer towards actually being at a desk and having to reach for various functions. I feel like that would enable spatial memory to do some cool things. I miss the 90s chunkiness of switches, buttons, hardware: being able to hear the computer "think" (HDD seeks), the hum of a CRT. Modern machinery feels so insubstantial, emphasizing clean glass and tidy machined chassis. (chassies?) I have this persistent da...

[bmurphy1976]: I want more stuff like this.  The era 20 years ago (e.g. Enlightenment) was way more fun than the bland monotonic design we have these days.  If you like bland modern design, great, that should be an option as well, but we should still have good variety.

[yldreader]: The entire concept of skeuomorphism on computers is nonsensical. A monitor has a default blank grey or black appearance. EVERYTHING else is skeuomorphic, including the ugly 'modern' color rectangles the people who use this word want to exempt.

[andai]: This warms my heart. I was just thinking about this the other week, when I bought an old iPhone, from the skeumorphic era, for nostalgic purposes. I've wanted one for years -- I only had the newer ones that were flat. I always thought, nah, I'm just seeing thru rose tinted glasses, surely it wasn't  that  cool, I'm gonna be disappointed... Well, I finally got one, and oh boy. It's even better than I imagined. There's just so much love and care put into the design...

[d1l]: The main difficulty I see in these "RETVRN TO SOVL" things is not the window-manager or desktop itself but the UI toolkits for the applications. GTK2 had so many excellent themes. Now GTK or libadwaita seem designed to resist themes and introduce constant breaking of selectors or widgets or whatnot. I believe they griefed the themers into just giving up. I have less knowledge about Qt, but I assume it's probably the better pick these days.

items.author: Jacob Lyon
items.content:
FBI helps smash crypto scam targeting Russian speakers in Brooklyn
The FBI has helped take down a crypto scam network that targeted Russian-speaking individuals living in the US and likely stole tens of millions of dollars.
The operation, described as “one of the biggest operational cyber disruptions undertaken by a local prosecutor’s office,” was led by Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez’s Virtual Currency Unit (VCU).
Russian-speaking people living in Brooklyn were targeted by crypto scammers operating a phony forex investment site that promised substantial returns via Russian-tailored ads.
Read more: Elliptic chief: Tether and Telegram prop up $442B scam economy
Individuals were contacted by fake investment advisors and convinced into depositing funds on their supposed investment site.
Victims were shown fake gains, and when they tried to withdraw their funds, they were told their account was locked or that they had to pay more money to access it.
Crypto scammers hit victims with more recovery scams
Authorities dismantled 241 crypto scam domains and 112 servers across Ukraine, Eastern Europe, and America.
The group would also revisit individuals it had already scammed, luring them with recovery operations that promised to restore their stolen crypto.
Gonzalez’s local office was able to seize $300,000, but despite this, many Individuals lost their life savings.
FBI director’s Russia optics aren’t great right now
FBI Director Kash Patel is also making headlines in relation to Russia.
MS NOW reported that Patel had landed in Russia on Wednesday for a two-day meeting with the country’s Federal Security Service (FSB).
However, US authorities clarified that he was in fact attending a law enforcement event in Virginia on that day.
Patel then posted on X, “From Russia, with love…” after the event.
Read more: Crypto hacking group ShinyHunters says it stole data of 5,000 FBI agents
This received considerable backlash, with X users highlighting the different ways the US is currently helping Russia.
Russia and the US recently signed a deal that would see Ukraine’s attacker trade 300,000 barrels of diesel with the US. The US is also slated to get a further 500,000 in November, and a million “immediately thereafter.”
Got a tip? Send us an email securely via Protos Leaks. For more informed news and investigations, follow us on X, Bluesky, and Google News, or subscribe to our YouTube channel.
items.title: FBI helps smash crypto scam targeting Russian speakers in Brooklyn

items.author: Ryan Gladwin
items.content:
In brief
- Privacy cryptocurrency Zcash has tanked 11% over the past 24 hours.
- Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, says this drop was likely caused by a build up in leverage after the token's "meteoric rise" in recent months.
- Another expert says that growing concerns that AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers might've prompted losses for Zcash.
Privacy-focused cryptocurrency Zcash has fallen 11% over the past 24 hours to a market capitalization of $18.5 billion, per Decrypt data, making it one of the biggest losers of the day.
One expert says this drop in valuation comes after its price has soared in recent months, which has led to a build up in leverage and amplified losses. Others say that growing concerns that AI can break cryptography faster than quantum computers are causing the privacy token to take bigger losses.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, highlighted that Zcash's "meteoric rise" means that it is still up 460% from its March lows and that in a "fragile" crypto market the largest gainers tend to take losses too.
"There was a decent build-up of leverage on the way up as this is also a natural consequence of a strong move," Nolan told Decrypt. "More attention brings more perp traders to take on leverage, and when there is a sneeze, the moves get amplified as those leveraged traders are either forced to reduce exposure or get liquidated."
Over the past 24 hours, per CoinGlass data, $17.9 million worth of Zcash long positions were liquidated, a large figure compared to Hyperliquid's $7.3 million over the same period.
The race to quantum-proof Zcash
The price drop comes as other industry-wide concerns start to swirl, some of which could see positive upside for Zcash.
Last week, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned that the industry needs to plan for "bunker mode" as AI could break crypto encryption before quantum computers do. The conversation was sparked after OpenAI published major progress in math, which presented concerns for the future of encryption.
"The OpenAI math breakthroughs has caused a lot concern in crypto given the conspicuous lack of cryptography proofs," Ryan Zurrer, founder and director of investment firm Dialectic, told Decrypt. "More complex privacy protocols such as Zcash have the most to lose in a zero-day event if core primitives are rendered obsolete against AI-driven cryptography attacks."
Zcash has been aggressive with its quest to quantum-proof the network. Zakura, a Zcash full node developer, recently said that its team expects to be quantum-proofed as well as reasonably AI-proofed by January. Its quantum-resistant roadmap "served as a key catalyst" for its recent rally, Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt. "Although actual implementation is still some distance away, it indeed reflects the market's continuous focus on the privacy sector since the beginning of this year."
Privacy continues to be a major crypto industry talking point. Sun added that as traditional finance continues to merge with the crypto industry, the need for privacy will continue to rise.
"As an increasing volume of traditional financial assets and operations migrate on-chain, privacy protection will no longer be merely an optional add-on," Sun told Decrypt, "but rather a fundamental prerequisite for financial institutions adopting blockchain technology."
Last week, French lawmakers progressed a law proposal that would require citizens to report crypto holdings equal to or above €100,000 ($112,000), or otherwise face a penalty. The proposed law received significant backlash in the wake of a wave of crypto-related "wrench attacks," robberies, and kidnappings across the country. Although the law hasn't passed yet, some have looked to privacy protocols as government oversight looms.
Nolan from CoinShares highlights that investors should zoom out when looking at Zcash's recent performance, pushing back on recent narratives pushing its price down.
"I think the French proposed law had little to do with the move, and in my view, it's simply a larger pullback given the meteoric rise," Nolan told Decrypt. "When you put the drawdown in context on the daily chart, even though it's been 35%+, it looks like a blip in comparison to the upmove."

How Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI took down a massive crypto fraud network targeting Russian speakers
The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.
- Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized or disrupted 241 scam websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto fraud that targeted Russian speakers in the US.
- The scheme allegedly stole tens of millions through Russian-language Facebook ads and fake advisers, then went after victims again with fake recovery offers.
- Officials have seized about $300,000 so far. Crypto scams made up roughly 84% of the investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025.
Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI have seized or disrupted 241 websites and 112 servers tied to a crypto investment scam that allegedly stole tens of millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims in the U.S.
The operation, carried out last week, came after a three-year investigation into a fraud network that relied on online infrastructure and IP addresses in Ukraine and other Eastern European countries, Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said. No arrests were announced.
The scammers drew victims through Russian-language Facebook ads that promised investment opportunities. Fake advisers then called the victims and coached them to buy cryptocurrency and send it to fraudulent trading platforms.
When victims tried to withdraw their funds, the platforms locked their accounts or demanded more payments for supposed taxes and fees.
The scammers then “tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Gonzalez said. Recovered data showed they contacted victims a few weeks after the initial fraud, offering to retrieve the stolen funds.
The DA’s Virtual Currency Unit had previously seized or disrupted 400 domains tied to crypto investment fraud, but replacement sites kept appearing.
This time, investigators targeted the servers, hosted by Eastern European and U.S. companies, that held victim data and the software used to run the fraud. The goal was to stop the operators from quickly launching new sites.
The case comes as crypto investment scams accounted for roughly 84% of the $8.65 billion in investment-fraud losses reported to the FBI in 2025, according to the bureau’s annual report.
Across all internet-crime categories, crypto-linked losses totaled $11.37 billion, approximately 54% of the $20.88 billion overall. Both percentages are calculated from the FBI’s totals.
Brooklyn authorities have seized about $300,000 and are working to recover more. Prosecutors said some victims lost their entire life savings.

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据彭博社报道，Ripple 旗下主经纪商部门 Ripple Prime 正面向机构客户推出现实世界资产（RWA）永续合约，覆盖股票、指数、ETF、大宗商品等 100 多个参考市场。该产品通过 Hyperliquid 上的 Trade.xyz 提供，延续了 Ripple Prime 此前向客户开放加密永续合约交易的布局。

items.content:
HEX token sellers erase $160M following reports of founder Richard Schueler arrest
The HEX token’s price declined by 30% following local media reports of the Istanbul arrest of founder Richard Schueler, nearly two years after Interpol issued a “Red Notice.”
The Hex (HEX) token fell nearly 30% in the past 24 hours after local media reports of founder Richard Schueler, also known as Richard Heart, being detained by authorities in Istanbul.
The HEX token declined to $0.0006 as of 11:28 am UTC on Thursday, erasing about $160 million from its market capitalization, from more than $500 million on Wednesday to $340 million by press time, according to CoinMarketCap. It previously topped $0.44 in September 2021.
On Wednesday, news outlet Ihlas Haber Ajansı (IHA) reported that Schueler and his wife were detained in Istanbul by Turkish authorities. Police reportedly seized multiple devices, hardware wallets, jewelry and handguns.
The reported arrest comes nearly two years after the world’s largest international police organization, Interpol, issued a “Red Notice” for Schueler for allegedly committing tax fraud and assault, with Finnish authorities seeking his arrest.
A spokesperson for Finland’s National Bureau of Investigations declined to comment on the matter.
Schueler was also listed on Europe’s most wanted fugitives list on similar allegations, claiming that he “physically assaulted a 16-year-old victim by grabbing their hair, dragging them into the stairwell and knocking them to the ground.”
In July 2023, the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) sued Schueler, alleging he raised $1 billion in an unregistered securities offering and misappropriated at least $12 million.
US District Judge Carol Bagley Amon dismissed the case in February 2025, after ruling that the activities were not sufficiently directed at US investors. In April 2025, the SEC said it didn’t intend to refile its securities fraud complaint against Schueler.

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors fall 3-5% after hot CPI; BTC at $80.9k
- Over $900M liquidated as crypto majors selloff; alts down 5-15%
- Solana sets Oct 21 for Alpenglow on mainnet

🏎️ Solana Cuts Finality From 12.8 Seconds to 150 Milliseconds
Next Wednesday, Solana rips out the engine and drops in a new one while the car is doing 70 on the highway.
On October 21, around 15:00 UTC, Solana activates Alpenglow on mainnet, retiring the consensus mechanism it has run on since launch. Finality drops from roughly 12.8 seconds to a target of about 150 milliseconds – 85 times faster. Anza, the core dev shop behind it, called it “18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot.”
Finality is the moment a transaction stops being reversible, the point where you can hand over the goods knowing the payment can’t be clawed back. Solana has always felt instant, but there was a roughly 13-second window where a block could in theory still get dropped. Every exchange and payment processor has had to build around that window. Next week it closes.
The old system breaks if more than about a third of staked SOL turns hostile. The new one is built to survive 20% of stake acting maliciously plus another 20% simply offline, and keep finalizing. For a chain whose reputation was built on outages, that’s the number institutions will actually care about.
Now the part that’s going to cause trouble. Validators currently cast their votes as transactions on the chain. Under Alpenglow they vote directly to each other instead, which means Solana’s headline transaction count and TPS figures are about to fall off a cliff. Nothing real changes - same users, same volume, same apps - but the number everyone has quoted for years was mostly validators voting at each other. Expect a wave of “Solana activity collapses” posts next Wednesday from people reading a dashboard.
This is also just phase one of two, and the second piece has no date yet. And Solana has missed an Alpenglow date before - a September 28 activation was announced, then pushed. So, grains of salt.
But clearly Solana is focused on speed as one of its primary differentiators - and it’s about to get a lot faster…

Ledger’s answer to wallet tampering costs $849 and ships next year
Ledger’s new Atom combines crypto wallet security with everyday apps and is expected to ship in summer 2027 as the company investigates tampered wallets sold in Asia.
Ledger unveiled a new device on Thursday with stronger protections against tampering, days after confirming that wallets sold through a reseller in Asia contained malicious implants.
The French hardware wallet maker introduced Atom, an $849 device that combines a crypto wallet with everyday apps through a smartphone-like design. Atom separates Android apps from sensitive wallet operations and includes protections Ledger says would block the implants used in the recent Asia incident. It’s also advertised to detect tampering even when switched off.
The company expects to begin shipping the device in summer 2027, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph.
Ledger said Atom will also support AI agent approvals, encrypted messaging and post-quantum cryptography.
The announcement follows a security incident that surfaced on Friday involving malicious implants found in wallets sold through authorized reseller CryptoBilis. Ledger has requested that distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong suspend sales of its products. European retail chain MediaMarkt has also pulled Ledger wallets off its shelves.
Asked when Atom’s anti-tampering protections were developed, a Ledger spokesperson said the work was not a response to isolated incidents. The spokesperson did not provide a development timeline.
In a separate blog post on Thursday, Ledger said it had introduced new rules requiring authorized resellers to keep devices off display and hand them to customers at purchase. It also reiterated that returned devices must never be resold.

items.author: AI Boost
items.content:
Under pressure, Ledger unveils plan to turn its crypto hardware wallet into a smartphone
Ledger’s Atom will run apps like WhatsApp and Instragram and let users switch between smartphone functions and a protected mode for managing digital assets.
- Ledger’s Atom, scheduled for release in mid-2027, will run apps like WhatsApp and Instragram and let users switch between smartphone functions and a protected mode for managing digital assets.
- The device will include tamper-resistant enclosures, sensors and packaging intended to prevent supply-chain attacks like the recent CryptoBilis breach, even when switched off.
- Ledger initially plans to sell Atom only through its website to limit third-party distribution risks, but it will not offer trade-ins for customers affected by the breach.
Cryptocurrency hardware wallet maker Ledger said it is developing a new device that looks and functions more like a smartphone than a traditional wallet.
The Ledger Atom, scheduled for release in mid-2027, marks a departure from the industry’s emphasis on safeguarding digital assets on minimalist devices meant to be locked away in a drawer or a desk.
The Atom runs Android, meaning users will be able to install everyday applications like WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok. Users can switch between ordinary smartphone functionality and a protected mode for managing digital assets. The device also incorporates integration with the AI assistant OpenClaw.
The product will be manufactured at Ledger’s location in Vietnam, as is customary with its more complex devices.
The Atom announcement comes amid fallout from a supply-chain security breach involving Malaysian distributor CryptoBilis, in which attackers reportedly tampered with devices before they reached customers. Onchain researchers estimated losses of up to $93.2 million across more than 300 wallets, with Tether freezing $10 million of its dollar-pegged stablecoin USDT tied to the theft.
The compromised wallets allegedly contained hidden chips capable of intercepting users’ 24-word recovery phrases — the stream of random words that only the owner of the wallet should know as the ultimate safeguard to their digital assets — by reading signals from their screens.
The incident largely affected users in Southeast Asia, with Ledger citing research on Wednesday to show no loss of funds reported in Europe.
Ledger says Atom will incorporate additional protections specifically designed to counter this type of attack, a spokesperson told CoinDesk via email. The safeguards include a protective enclosure around the device’s most sensitive components, sensors that detect attempts to remove its screen or back cover and packaging designed to reveal whether it has been opened.
The tamper-detection system has its own battery to ensure it functions even if the device is switched off.
“The Core protection enclosure will explicitly block the screen reader implants from this weekend’s incident,” the spokesperson said.
Ledger plans to initially sell the device exclusively through its own website rather than through third-party sellers, in theory reducing exposure to distribution channels implicated in the CryptoBilis incident.
The company also said it has no plans to introduce trade-in programs for existing customers affected by the incident, though it does not rule out future upgrade promotions.
The concept of combining smartphone functionality with hardware-level crypto security isn’t entirely new. Solana introduced its Saga smartphone in 2023, followed by its successor, Seeker, last year. Both featured built-in hardware protection for private keys. Ledger is approaching this idea from the opposite direction, by starting with a crypto security device and turning it into something resembling an everyday smartphone.
UPDATE (Oct. 15, 12:05 UTC): Adds the location of Atom’s manufacturing and references research on CryptoBilis incident not showing any loss of funds in Europe.

items.ai_reason: A first-instance acquittal in a high-profile $230M (340 billion KRW) Korean crypto fraud case involving the POD and ATT tokens. This is a notable legal/enforcement signal for Korean crypto prosecution standards — the court found the causal link between alleged false promotion and investor losses unproven, and price manipulation/embezzlement charges unsupported. It is legally significant but does not change market access, rules, or industry structure, so it sits in the 'interesting, worth knowing' band rather than high-impact regulatory change.

中国台湾地区封锁Coinbase及Kalshi网站，指其涉嫌违反选举博彩规定

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据彭博社报道，中国台湾地区因涉嫌选举博彩，已封锁 Coinbase 及 Kalshi 网站。新北市一家法院已授权当地通信监管机构及互联网注册管理机构限制访问上述平台。部分中国台湾 Coinbase 用户表示，自周三起已无法访问网站。

申请封锁令的中国台湾刑事警察局表示，上述网站涉嫌违反《公职人员选举罢免法》，该法禁止依据选举或罢免结果经营营利性赌博业务。该部门称，限制措施旨在维护选举公正并防止「境外干预」，但未提供更多细节。Coinbase 和 Kalshi 尚未回应置评请求。

相关限制出台于 11 月 28 日地方选举前。根据 2023 年修订的相关法律，参与选举博彩者最高可面临 6 个月监禁，经营者最高可面临 5 年监禁。预测市场平台 Polymarket 也已在中国台湾地区被封锁。

Pendle高收益USDC金库上线不足一日存款规模突破1600万美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，Pendle 宣布，其在 Morpho 上的 Pendle 生态系统高收益 USDC 金库，上线不到一天 TVL 即突破 1600 万美元。Morpho 页面显示，截至目前，该金库存款总额已达约 1602 万美元，净 APY 为 8.19%。

该金库由 Pendle 与 Wintermute 旗下金库管理业务 Armitage 共同管理，与原有 Pendle Ecosystem USDC 金库并行运行。目前，Pendle 在 Morpho 已有两个 USDC 生态金库。

相比原有金库，新金库覆盖更广泛的 PT 市场，将 USDC 流动性配置至选定的高收益 PT 抵押借贷市场，为 PT 循环借贷用户提供更多借款流动性。Pendle 表示，相关借款需求支撑金库收益，进而吸引更多存款。

items.author: Decrypt Agent
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin dipped to an intraday low under $81,000, extending losses after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data revived bets on a Fed rate hike.
- HashKey's Tim Sun said slowing demand from spot ETFs and corporate Bitcoin treasuries explains the stalled rally more than macro factors alone.
- Algoz's Stephen Wundke expects Bitcoin to trade between $76,000 and $83,000 for the rest of October unless a clear catalyst emerges.
Bitcoin dipped below $81,000 on Thursday, extending its slide a day after U.S. consumer prices rose faster than expected and revived bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike.
The leading cryptocurrency is currently trading at $81,002, per CoinGecko data, down 2.7% over the past 24 hours and 2.5% over the past week, after slipping to an intraday low of $80,444.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year to September, Decrypt reported on Wednesday. Prices rose 0.6% over the month, the largest monthly increase in five months, driven mainly by energy costs tied to the war with Iran, The New York Times reported.
Traders' odds of a Fed rate hike this month jumped to 43% from 24% after the report, the Times said, though federal funds futures still point to December for the next increase. The Fed raised rates to a range of 3.75% to 4% in September.
CME FedWatch put the odds of an October hike at 29.3% on Thursday, up from 17.7% a week earlier, while traders on prediction markets Myriad and Polymarket priced it at 28%. Polymarket traders put the chance of a December hike at 79%. (Disclosure: Myriad is a prediction market operated by Decrypt's parent company, Dastan.)
Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, argued that those probabilities feed directly into Bitcoin's price. "On the bullish side as long as BTC stays above $79,500 we can keep the dream alive," Wundke told Decrypt.
Inflation has now run above the Fed's 2% target for 66 straight monthly readings, the longest streak this century, according to a CNBC analysis. "They're starting to accept high inflation as just a fact of life," Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wrote in a LinkedIn post last week.
Those pressures are only part of the picture, Tim Sun of HashKey Group told Decrypt. Rising rate hike expectations, a stronger dollar and a pullback in AI tech stocks have weighed on Bitcoin on the surface, he said, "however, the deeper reason lies in the changing structure of incremental capital."
"Over the last two years, the key marginal buyers of Bitcoin primarily came from spot ETFs and corporate Bitcoin treasuries," Sun said. As borrowing costs rise, narrowing valuation premiums at some corporate treasuries have made it less attractive to raise money to keep buying Bitcoin, he added.
"Nevertheless, Bitcoin has not experienced a sustained deep sell-off as a result," Sun said, pointing to growing involvement from major traditional banks that has added long-term capital to the market.
Bitcoin's trading range
Sun expects Bitcoin to stay range-bound in the short term. A breakout depends on whether ETF flows return to sustained net inflows and whether corporate treasuries can improve their ability to raise money and buy, he said.
Wundke also expects a range. "Without a clear catalyst to move things higher I fear we are range bound with BTC between $76,000 and $83,000 for the rest of October," he said, adding that peace with Iran "would change that dynamic instantly."
"In the short term Bitcoin trades as a liquidity asset, and higher for longer means tighter liquidity, so this drop is the market repricing rates, not a change in Bitcoin's story," Abdul Rafay Gadit, co-founder of ZIG Finance, told Decrypt.
"The next few weeks are about the Fed, not crypto," Gadit said. "If it signals it can look through sticky inflation, risk appetite returns quickly; if not, expect choppy trading."
The Fed will announce its next rate decision on October 28.

分析师：比特币或回调下探至74,600美元，中期趋势仍偏多

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，加密分析师 Darkfost 发文表示，比特币技术面判断未出现实质变化，第Ⅰ浪中的第（5）子浪已在预期位置结束，接下来或迎来第Ⅱ浪调整。该调整浪可能下探至 74,600 美元，对应通常的 0.382 斐波那契回撤位。

目前，比特币已跌破 21 周期 EMA，正处于 50 周期 EMA 支撑位，后者被其视为较强支撑；200 周期 EMA 则位于约 75,800 美元，距离当前价格仍有一定空间。

RSI 已回到 50 的中性水平，但与 14 周期 SMA 的差距扩大。Darkfost 认为，这意味着在最后一轮 C 浪到来前，可能先出现 B 浪修正性反弹。他表示，当前暂无值得担忧的信号，比特币中期趋势仍偏积极。

items.author: theblockbeats
items.content:
Midjourney工程师开源Handwired：不用训练，直接把程序规则写成神经网络

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Midjourney 工程师 Cheng Lou 开源了 Handwired，给神经网络换了一种造法。

GPT 等大模型需要通过大量数据训练，才能确定内部权重。Handwired 则直接根据 JavaScript 的计算规则设定权重。神经网络本质上由一层层数学运算组成，权重就是其中的数字系数。既然程序规则已经写好了，就可以直接构造对应的计算结构，省去训练过程。

比如，代码规定整数大于 4 就返回 10，否则返回 12。Handwired 用 ReLU 和乘法构造一个代表真假的数字开关，代替原本的 if-else 判断。循环、状态更新也能拆成类似的数值运算。

Cheng Lou 用这套方法做出了浏览器迷你桌面，130 层计算、9909 个权重负责窗口拖动、缩放、动画和照片布局。整个过程无需训练，普通 CPU 就能运行，界面仍由浏览器负责绘制。

单纯为了实现这些功能，直接写 JavaScript 更方便。但 Handwired 让固定的程序规则和可训练的参数共用一套计算结构。程序可以继续按照规则执行，需要调整的部分则能通过反向传播，根据结果的误差修改权重。

照片排版演示就利用了这个特点。用户随手画出照片的大致位置，系统便持续训练一个只有 244 个权重的小网络，让照片尽量贴近目标位置，并自动对齐边缘。固定的交互规则照常执行，排版参数则在实时学习。

Cheng Lou 还提出，可以把这种固定规则模块接进 nanoGPT。如今大模型也能调用外部程序完成精确计算，但外部代码通常无法直接参与模型的反向传播。

如果把程序规则写成兼容的计算图，就有机会让模型同时使用预先确定的规则和通过训练获得的能力，甚至联合优化其中可训练的部分。

目前这仍是早期实验。Handwired 还不能自动转换任意 JavaScript，开发者需要手工构建计算图，部分条件判断也无法直接获得有用的梯度。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372051

Surf在Robinhood Chain推出SurfBoard NFT，开图后可累积代币化美股

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，AI 加密研究平台 Surf 在 Robinhood Chain 上线 NFT 系列 SurfBoard，总量 6666 个，不增发、无公开发售且团队零预留。符合条件的年度会员可免费领取，其他用户可通过官网以 1 枚 $SURFBOARD 购买未开图 NFT。

SurfBoard 采用 ERC-404 标准，开图后将根据稀有度权重，累积 NVDA、SPY、META、GOOGL 和 SPCX 五种代币化股票。收益资金来自官方池 3% 的交易手续费（其中 2.2125% 用于买入股票）及已开图 NFT 5% 的二级市场版税。持有人可出售 NFT 并将累积奖励一并转让，也可销毁 NFT 赎回 95% 的奖励，剩余 5% 按权重分配给其他已开图 NFT。

官网数据显示，截至发稿，已有 1916 个 SurfBoard 完成开图，占总量约 29%，累计计入股票价值约 2 万美元，未开图 NFT 现价约 200 美元。Surf 提醒，$SURFBOARD 仅支持在官方平台交易，其他 DEX 报价均来自非官方池。

Runway让Agent边干活边生成视频：代码仓库变小镇，文件操作也能看

动察 Beating AI 快讯，Runway 旗下实验团队 Runway Labs 展示了 Visual Thinking，可以把 AI Agent 的工作过程实时变成视频。

Agent 搜索网页、调用工具、读取或修改文件时，视频模型会根据这些操作同步生成画面。用户不必逐条翻看执行日志，就能直观看到 Agent 正在做什么。

比如，让 Agent 解释一个 monorepo（多个项目共用的代码仓库），系统会把代码库画成一座小镇。不同程序包像货物一样运往各个应用，文档则变成河边的公园。Agent 访问或修改文件夹时，画面也会随之变化。

另一个演示中，Agent 在户型图上模拟 Wi-Fi 信号传播，找出覆盖死角并展示调整方案。就连挑选礼物时的网页搜索和工具调用，也能变成动态画面。

Visual Thinking 并非独立产品，而是 Runway 新操作系统研究项目 Continuum 的一项功能。Continuum 早在 10 月 1 日就已亮相，这次主要展示更多应用场景。

目前仍处于研究演示阶段，尚未开放公开试用。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372046

欧洲银行管理局将USDC认定为欧盟首个「重要电子货币代币」

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，欧洲银行管理局（EBA）宣布，根据《加密资产市场法规》（MiCA），将 Circle 发行的 USDC 认定为「重要电子货币代币」。USDC 由此成为欧盟已通报的 45 种电子货币代币中，首个达到该认定标准的代币。

自 11 月 12 日起，EBA 将直接负责 USDC 自有资金、储备资产、流动性要求，以及恢复与赎回计划的监管。这些领域目前由法国审慎监管与处置局（ACPR）负责。移交后，ACPR 仍将负责公司治理、合格持股、适当性评估及利益冲突等事项。

EBA 还表示，已与纽约州金融服务局（NYDFS）签署谅解备忘录，以促进跨境监管及信息交换。NYDFS 负责监督 Circle 在纽约州受监管的业务。据 The Block 数据，USDC 供应量接近 730 亿美元，为全球第二大稳定币。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，据《财富》报道，代币化基金流动性平台 Fission 宣布完成 1000 万美元 A 轮融资，由 Pantera Capital 领投，Circle Ventures、Borderless Capital 及 Ari Rubenstein 参投。本轮融资于 9 月完成，公司未披露估值。

Fission 旨在解决代币化基金份额难以快速变现的问题。平台通过充当买方，让投资者出售份额，而不必等待基金处理赎回。用户连接数字钱包并提交出售请求，Fission 负责后台法律及交易流程。CEO Jonathan Shaffer 表示，对于通常需约 200 天才能出售的产品，投资者可支付费用立即出售，并在 90 秒或更短时间内完成结算。

Fission 于 2024 年成立，创始团队包括 Point72 和 Securitize 前员工。目前客户主要为机构投资者及持有链上资产的组织，包括持有代币化私募信贷或股权资产的对冲基金、管理财库的加密机构，以及将储备配置于生息代币化投资产品的稳定币发行商。

items.content:
传DeepSeek再投机器人创业公司：前逐际动力基模负责人创业，估值或达2亿美元

动察 Beating AI 快讯，DeepSeek 再被曝拟投资具身智能创业公司。Top 华人科创社获悉，逐际动力前人形机器人基础模型负责人俞涛已离职创业，方向为 LLM 与具身智能结合。据相关人士透露，新公司首轮估值约 7000 万美元，第二轮约 2 亿美元，DeepSeek 也在潜在投资方之列。目前，公司名称、实际融资金额及交易进度均未披露。

俞涛拥有中科大博士学位，此前曾在腾讯 AI Lab 绝悟团队研究强化学习，随后负责逐际动力的人形机器人基础模型。他带队研发的 System 0 主要解决机器人的全身运动控制问题。比如机器人弯腰捡箱子时，不仅要伸手抓取，还得协调双腿、腰部和手臂，实时调整重心，避免摔倒。逐际动力今年 7 月公布的 COSA 0.5 已将这套技术用于 43 自由度人形机器人 Oli，支持边行走边操作，并通过真机强化学习改进动作策略。

DeepSeek 的投资动作正在向物理世界延伸。今年 8 月，它斥资约 1.41 亿元参与宇树科技 IPO 战略配售，承诺锁定 36 个月。10 月 12 日，彭博社又披露，DeepSeek 拟领投前腾讯科学家胡瀚创办的 Winverse AI，投后估值约 4 亿美元，但交易尚未敲定。凤凰网科技同期获悉，梁文锋正密集接触具身智能创业者，评估自建团队和外部投资两种路线。

这几项动作指向不同的技术环节。宇树提供机器人硬件与合作场景，胡瀚拥有视觉语言和具身基础模型研发经验，俞涛则擅长将模型生成的动作真正落实到机器人全身控制。如果最新投资落地，DeepSeek 将进一步接触机器人的底层执行技术。

items.content:
HTX DeepThink：CPI冲击后杠杆仍在累积，加密市场去杠杆风险上升

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 15 日，HTX DeepThink 专栏作者、HTX Research 研究员 Chloe 分析指出，美国 9 月 CPI 带来的冲击已从利率预期调整扩散至整体风险偏好，而衍生品市场的去杠杆尚未完成，加密市场短期仍面临下行压力。数据公布后，美债收益率一度快速上行，随后涨幅部分回落，加密市场跌势却仍在延续，截至北京时间 10 月 15 日 12:00，BTC 累计下跌 3.50%，ETH 下跌 6.27%。

从历史数据看，CPI 对加密市场的冲击主要集中在短期。过去 18 次 CPI 发布中，通胀超预期幅度与发布后 30 分钟内 BTC 收益的相关系数为 -0.46，到 4 小时和 24 小时分别降至 -0.14 和 -0.09。宏观数据给出初始方向，后续走势更多取决于流动性、机构资金与杠杆结构。本次数据发布后 30 分钟内，BTC 成交额放大约 5 倍，83,000 美元附近的初始承接仍未能阻止下跌；BTC 现货 ETF 近六个交易日累计净流出约 8.59 亿美元，现货支撑进一步削弱。

衍生品数据同样显示杠杆尚未出清。CPI 发布后 4 小时内，主要币种未平仓合约普遍增加，其中，截至次日中午 SOL 未平仓合约增长 7.95%，说明下跌过程中杠杆风险仍在积累。

未来 1 至 3 天，市场整体或维持谨慎偏空。BTC 可能受空头回补推动反弹至 81,600 美元附近，但在美元强势、ETF 资金流出与核心通胀压力未缓解的背景下，仍有重新测试 80,200 美元的风险；若跌破该位置并伴随未平仓合约快速下降，可能触发进一步去杠杆。83,860 美元是判断本轮 CPI 冲击是否被充分消化的重要参考位置，短期内山寨币的下行弹性预计继续高于 BTC。

注：本文内容并非投资意见，亦不构成任何投资产品之要约、要约招揽或建议。

原文链接 https://m.theblockbeats.info/flash/372040
