items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
Organizations join forces to fight Illinois crypto tax, after 6-month pause
Illinois officials already agreed to delay implementation of a 0.2% tax on crypto assets, but industry-aligned organizations are pushing for summary judgment on the merits.
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) and Blockchain Association (BA) said they would join the Digital Chamber and others to push for a court to address the merits of a lawsuit over Illinois’s digital-asset tax, set to take effect in 2027.
In a Tuesday filing in the Circuit Court of Sangamon County, the crypto advocacy organizations asked the court to approve an expedited schedule for summary judgment “to reach a decision on the tax’s lawfulness as quickly as possible.” The filing cited the CCI’s and BA’s lawsuit against Illinois state officials, as well as one filed separately by the Digital Chamber and Illinois Blockchain Association.
“While pausing enforcement of the Digital Asset Tax Act protects Illinois consumers and businesses from this onerous and legally flawed tax until July 1, it remains imperative that the merits are determined as soon as possible,” said CCI CEO Ji Kim.
Earlier this month, Illinois officials agreed to delay implementation of the 0.2% crypto tax law for six months, from Jan. 1 to July 1, 2027. The decision, part of the Digital Chamber’s lawsuit, came in response to claims that the digital asset tax had been “slipped into the state’s budget” without debate or public feedback. Digital Chamber CEO Cody Carbone said at the time that the organization would continue with legal proceedings “until this tax is struck down for good.”
Related: French lawmakers back stablecoin swap tax in 2027 budget bill
The expedited schedule, subject to court approval, could allow a decision on the merits of the law by March.
Leadership shakeup at Blockchain Association this week
On Friday, Summer Mersinger is scheduled to step down as CEO of the Blockchain Association as part of a leadership transition. Mersinger joined the advocacy group last year after resigning from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Kristin Smith, the organization’s former CEO, will step in as interim head, though Mersinger is expected to stay on until the end of 2026.

items.content:
In brief
- Autonomous AI agents have made over 138 million crypto payments through Coinbase’s x402 protocol on Base, per Chainalysis, as “agentic commerce” emerges as one of crypto’s fastest-growing use cases.
- The payments are tiny—87%+ fell between a hundredth of a cent and 10 cents—the kind of micro-transactions stablecoins handle but card rails can’t.
- The boom rides maturing infrastructure from Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase and Google, though earlier research suggests much agent activity may be scripts, not genuine agents.
AI agents are beginning to spend real money, and increasingly they’re paying in crypto.
That’s the picture from a new Chainalysis report, which found that autonomous AI agents have made more than 138 million cryptocurrency payments through x402, the Coinbase-incubated protocol that lets software pay for online services automatically.
The report, part of the blockchain analytics firm’s annual Geography of Crypto series and focused on North America’s $3 trillion crypto economy, frames “agentic commerce” as one of the sector’s fastest-emerging use cases.
The growth has been steep. Cumulative payments through x402 on Base, Coinbase’s layer-2 network, rose from roughly 1,500 in mid-2025 to more than 138 million by the third quarter of 2026, as developers increasingly hand AI agents their own budgets to buy computing power, live web data and coding tools on the fly. The payments are tiny: more than 87% fell between a hundredth of a cent and 10 cents, the kind of micro-transaction stablecoins can handle but traditional card rails cannot.
The United States dominates the activity. American-linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of geographically identifiable payments for AI model inference, Chainalysis found, compared with just 0.1% for China, though Chinese-linked wallets made up the bulk of spending on security and code-analysis services.
The firm cautioned against reading too much into the gap, noting the figures capture only identifiable x402 activity rather than the entire global market.
The report lands as the infrastructure for agent payments rapidly matures. Visa, Mastercard and Stripe have all moved to support AI-agent payments, Coinbase rolled out a tool letting agents trade and transact and has begun letting business customers accept agent payments, and Google unveiled a dedicated agent-payments protocol.
BlackRock has flagged autonomous agents as a potential next wave of crypto demand, with the firm’s head of digital assets research, Will Su, telling Chainalysis the company is watching the space closely “with AI agents potentially creating meaningful demand for frequent, low-value payments around the clock.”
A note of caution, however, hangs over the numbers. Earlier research from rival crypto tracing company TRM suggested much of the apparent agent activity on these rails may be scripts or self-dealing rather than genuine autonomous agents, a reminder that raw transaction counts can overstate how much real agentic commerce is happening.
Still, the trajectory points one way, and the thesis increasingly floated across the industry is that crypto’s next wave of users may not be people at all.

Pseudonymous GTA 6 leaker “Cyberleek” has threatened to reveal the long-awaited game’s ending if they’re caught, but won’t be leaking content regularly anymore because of their poorly performing crypto token.
Last week, Protos reported that Cyberleek had ended their hiatus to drop more GTA 6 leaks with an emphasis on nudity.
It pumped their cryptocurrency by 200% over two days, which, despite the positive price action, wasn’t as good as the $40 million market cap it achieved when the first leaks were revealed.

Right now, the token’s market cap sits at a little over $1 million. It reportedly began to crash after they announced a roadmap of several million-dollar market cap leak milestones.
Cyberleek still threatens GTA 6 endgame spoilers
Despite this, Cyberleek still claims they can leak the game’s ending, and as evidence, claimed to show out-of-context clips of the final story missions.
Rather than leak it outright, they’ve threatened a “dead man’s switch” that will spoil the game’s ending if they’re ever caught.
They claim it would ruin the experience for gamers and that Rockstar Games’ parent company, Take-Two, “was punished enough.”
Read more: GTA VI leak investigation video raises crypto scam suspicions
GTA 6 is currently set to release on November 19.
People Make Games co-founder Chris Bratt claims that an employment tribunal between Rockstar Games and 34 fired workers was delayed by a month to November 17 and 18.
Bratt says this is because Rockstar Games asked for more time for its lawyers to cross-examine certain employees.

items.content:
In brief
- The Bank of Russia added Sberbank to its register of crypto exchange operators on October 12, six days after listing it as a digital depository.
- Sberbank plans to launch its first crypto products on December 1 inside SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, starting with Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT.
- Retail buyers face a 300,000 ruble annual cap per intermediary and a mandatory knowledge test, and paying for goods with crypto remains illegal in Russia.
The Bank of Russia has added Sberbank to its register of organizations authorized to exchange digital currencies, clearing the country's largest lender to buy and sell crypto in its own name and with its own money. The decision was posted on the regulator's website, Russian outlet Interfax reported.
The approval landed six days after the central bank put Sberbank on its separate list of digital depositories, the firms that keep the official record of who owns which coins. Holding both statuses lets the bank sit on the other side of a client's trade and also keep the ledger of that client's holdings, without sending anyone to an outside venue.
Sberbank said the depository status would let it offer crypto services in interfaces clients already use. That means SberBank Online, SberInvestments and SberBusiness, where the bank plans to start with Bitcoin, Ethereum and Tether's USDT on December 1, according to its press service.
The bank has hedged that date, saying it depends on the central bank's decisions and on the secondary regulations being ready in time. Both approvals by the Bank of Russia have now arrived, which leaves the secondary rulebook as the main variable.
Sberbank ended the second quarter with 110.6 million retail clients and 3.5 million corporate clients, per its quarterly results. Plugging crypto into that user base turns a regulated on-ramp into one more menu item inside an app those customers already use for everyday banking.
Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov has forecast that crypto trading volumes in Russia could reach 4 trillion rubles, roughly $46 billion, in the regime's first year and 7.5 trillion rubles by 2029 or nearly $89.7 billion. The bank also plans to accept Ethereum and USDT, alongside Bitcoin, as collateral for loans once the central bank allows them into public circulation.
Under the law Putin signed in August, non-qualified investors can spend up to 300,000 rubles (about $3,800) a year per intermediary, buyers must pass a knowledge test, and the central bank's draft list of tradable coins includes only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT.
In January 2022, the Bank of Russia proposed banning crypto use, mining and exchanges outright, citing threats to financial stability. Less than five years later, it is licensing the country's biggest lender to run a crypto desk. As of today, spending crypto inside Russia is still illegal, so Sberbank customers will be able to buy Bitcoin but not pay for products with it.
Firms already on the registers have until September 1, 2027, to bring their operations fully in line with the new law, the central bank said.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Alpenglow activates on Solana mainnet in epoch 1064, which starts on Wednesday, October 21, at approximately 15:00 UTC, according to the Solana Foundation.
- The upgrade replaces TowerBFT and targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, down from about 12.8 seconds today.
- Vote transactions will leave blocks, so Solana's headline transaction counts and TPS figures will drop sharply without any drop in real activity.
Solana has locked in October 21 for Alpenglow, a full replacement of the system its validators use to reach consensus. The switch is tied to epoch 1064, which the Solana Foundation expects to begin around 15:00 UTC that Wednesday.
Alpenglow retires TowerBFT, the current system the network uses, and aims to make transactions final in roughly 150 milliseconds. Finality is the moment a transaction becomes irreversible, and under TowerBFT that currently takes about 12.8 seconds.
On Solana today, a payment is confirmed pretty quickly, but that’s not a guarantee. Until TowerBFT runs out its 13 second clock, the block could in theory still be dropped.
That small doubt is why anyone handling real money tends to wait out the full window. With finality at around 150ms, the irreversible answer arrives almost as fast as the optimistic one, which is what a checkout counter taking SOL or a DeFI application, or a trading desk settling a position actually needs.
TowerBFT works by having validators post their votes as on-chain transactions, and a block only counts as final once 32 slots’ worth of those votes pile up. Votor, the voting protocol shipping with Alpenglow, takes votes off the chain, so validators message each other directly, package the votes into certificates, and can lock in a block after a single round of voting, or two at most.
When 80% or more of stake backs a block in the first round, it finalizes on the spot. If support lands between 60% and 80%, a second round with 60% thresholds decides whether the block is finalized or skipped, and the Foundation says the design tolerates 20% malicious stake plus another 20% offline.
It’s time.
Alpenglow goes live on mainnet-beta Wednesday, October 21, ~14:50 UTC.
18 months of work for a migration that happens in one slot. Finality drops from seconds to ~150ms.
Make sure to follow us @anza_xyz as we countdown to go-live.
Details: https://t.co/MEf26uzCMW
— Anza (@anza_xyz) October 13, 2026
Ordinary users don’t need to do anything, and wallets and apps should behave as they do now. The Solana Virtual Machine, transaction formats, programs, and fees are left alone, while for developers the “confirmed” and “finalized” commitment levels become one and the same.
Each vote account also needs 0.8 SOL on top of its rent-exempt balance to pay the new Validator Admission Ticket, a per-epoch fee of the same size that gets burned. It replaces the roughly 1 SOL per epoch validators spent on vote transaction fees under TowerBFT, and a validator that can’t cover it sits out voting and block production for the following epoch.
The feature gate turns on as epoch 1064 begins, yet TowerBFT stays in charge for another 5,000 slots, roughly 18 minutes, before Alpenglow takes control at slot 459,653,000. This assures stability and prevents any issues during transition.
Validators approved Alpenglow in September 2025, when the SIMD-0326 proposal passed with 98.27% of votes cast in favor. In May, Anza Lead Economist Max Resnick told Decrypt the team was looking at a late Q3 or early Q4 mainnet activation, so everything is going according to schedule.
October 21 delivers only Votor, the first half of Alpenglow. Rotor, a replacement for Turbine, the system Solana uses to broadcast block data between validators, comes later and still has no date.

Strategy’s USD Cash down 60% in seven weeks
USD Cash at Michael Saylor’s BTC treasury company Strategy has fallen 60% from $1.61 billion on August 30 to $640.5 million on October 11, according to its latest disclosure this week.
The firm has spent the majority of its USD Cash on STRC buybacks, Strategy’s ultra-high yield dividend stock that it sold to investors for $90–100.03 per share before those same shares briefly collapsed to $71.25.
Reinstilling confidence that the shares would trade near their intended $100 price has cost the company — especially common shareholders — extensive cash that the company mostly raised via common shareholder dilution.
Read more: Strategy’s USD reserve didn’t last long
Strategy’s pace of USD Cash depletion works out to about $970 million in less than seven weeks. If it continues that average pace and doesn’t top it up, its USD Cash will run out in about four weeks.
Amid the aforementioned buybacks, Saylor has taken to X to post glowing reviews about STRC’s recovery. This included another installment of his imaginary retiree supposedly enjoying a carefree lifestyle funded by STRC dividends.
Pretend to not check the price of STRC
The unbothered, AI-generated investor doesn’t even bother to check the price of STRC.
Although irresponsible, choosing to bury one’s head in the sand certainly would have saved any real investor the gut-punch of STRC’s actual price whipsawing 29% since Saylor first broadcasted her testimonial from his social media feed on March 30.
Read more: Strategy has burned through 64% of its STRC rescue fund
Strategy’s August USD Cash figure included expected proceeds from stock sales that hadn’t yet settled, but the starting figure is accurate by Strategy’s own accounting with that footnote.
Moreover, USD Cash isn’t Strategy’s only dollar stockpile, due to a separate “USD Reserve,” earmarked for bond coupons and dividend payments, holding $4.88 billion as of October 11.
That reserve is down from the $5.10 billion it reported for August 30.
The combined change of both USD reserves is still decidedly negative, albeit slightly less dramatically at approximately 18% combined.
Strategy’s two piles of USD cash
Strategy created USD Cash on August 24, funding most of it with about $1.57 billion from the sale of roughly $2 billion of MSTR stock the week prior.
Common shareholders, as usual, paid for Strategy executives’ flexibility by suffering dilution of their MSTR shares.
The company explained at the time, “USD Cash complements the USD Reserve by providing management with a more flexible source of liquidity for the purposes described above.”
In plain English, executives gave themselves a second pot of cash from which they could spend more freely.
The older USD Reserve had stricter limits. Strategy may use this reserve for preferred dividends and interest payments, unless its board formally authorizes otherwise.
It paid out $142.5 million for those purposes during the week of October 4, for example.
Strategy’s board doubled its STRC total buyback authorization to $2 billion in September, yet just $354.8 million of that authorized amount remained as of October 11.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
EU authority classifies Circle’s USDC as ‘significant’ under MiCA
The second-largest stablecoin by market cap will be overseen by French and EU authorities under its classification as a “significant e-money token.“
The European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle’s USDC stablecoin as a significant e-money token under the region’s Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework.
In a Wednesday notice, the banking regulator said the e-money token classification, granted to only 45 other projects, effectively means the USDC stablecoin will be jointly overseen by the EBA and France’s supervisory authority, the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution. The stablecoin is the second largest by market capitalization, at $73 billion compared to Tether USDt’s $184 billion.
The “significant“ classification came as many EU-based token issuers pushed for regulated US dollar-pegged stablecoins in the region. Stable Mint CEO James Bennett told Cointelegraph that while Europe couldn’t “wish away“ dollar stablecoins, regulators could control safeguards and rules for issuers.
“For European corporates to make cross-border payments globally, offering only a euro stablecoin isn’t enough,” AllUnity CEO Alexander Höptner told Cointelegraph.
As authorities and issuers move closer to embracing dollar stablecoins, policymakers at the European Central Bank continue to explore the potential introduction of a digital euro. The EU authority first proposed the central bank digital currency in 2020, with the potential to issue the coin in 2029 after the conclusion of legislation and a pilot program.
Related: Qivalis wins Dutch e-money license for euro stablecoin

items.content:
Bank of America hit with $1.2B fine after missing ‘Chinese money laundering’
Bank of America has been fined a total of $1.2 billion dollars by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) after admitting failures of its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program resulting in over $5 billion in suspicious activity.
The $750 million fine from the OCC is the largest civil money penalty that the bureau has ever issued.
FinCEN is responsible for the remainder of the fine and credits the $750 million against its total penalty of $1.2 billion.
Read more: How a money launderer allegedly used Deltec, Binance, and Tether
The FinCEN order details how Bank of America “willfully failed to implement and maintain adequate internal controls for BSA compliance” which resulted in missing or delayed reports for “over $5 billion of suspicious activity, with roughly $1 billion of this activity implicating national security-related and other priority illicit finance risks, including suspicious transactions indicative of Chinese Money Laundering Networks.”
This Chinese Money Laundering Network activity included “high volumes of back-to-back credit card purchases at major retailers and shipping companies inconsistent with customer profiles,” and “regular, large-value ACH and bill pay transactions to pay off balances for credit cards issued by third-party financial institutions.
These included “cards in the name of third-party individuals for which there was no apparent commercial purpose; large wire transfers to counterparties in China with generic descriptions (e.g., “for goods”) and no discernible business rationale; and substantial, repeated transfers to counterparties with no web presence operating from residential addresses, demonstrating an apparent lack of legitimate commercial purpose.”
Additionally, FinCEN found that the bank’s due diligence on correspondent accounts held by its own foreign branches and affiliates fell short.
Some regulatory questionnaires “were completed by the bank on behalf of all its foreign branches and affiliates, and others were completed for specific foreign branches and affiliates.”
This record-breaking OCC fine follows its recent $350 million fine levied against American Express.

US authorities dismantle crypto scam network that stole tens of millions
Brooklyn prosecutors and the FBI seized 112 servers and shut down 241 websites linked to investment scams that targeted Russian-speaking Americans.
Prosecutors in Brooklyn, New York, working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have disrupted an Eastern European cryptocurrency scam network accused of stealing tens of millions of dollars from Americans, primarily Russian-speakers.
The operation, carried out last week and announced on Wednesday, resulted in the shutdown of 241 websites and the seizure of 112 servers hosted by companies in Eastern Europe and the United States, according to the Brooklyn District Attorney’s Office. No arrests were made.
“These criminals stole many millions of dollars from Russian-speaking victims through an elaborate investment scheme, then tried to exploit them again with false promises to recover their money,” Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said in a statement. He credited the office’s Virtual Currency Unit and the FBI with uncovering the network’s infrastructure.
Seizing the servers was key to the operation because it disrupted the scammers’ ability to create new websites and contact victims. “We disabled the back end of the operation,” Assistant District Attorney Alona Katz, who led the investigation, said, according to Bloomberg.
The operation comes amid a rise in cryptocurrency-related fraud across the US. Americans reported $11.4 billion in crypto fraud losses in 2025, a 22% increase from the previous year, according to FBI figures cited by Bloomberg.

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- Standard Chartered launched direct Bitcoin and Ethereum trading for affluent UAE clients on Wednesday after receiving licensing approval from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority.
- Eligible Professional Investor clients can buy and sell BTC and ETH through their existing bank accounts, with the bank handling custody and settlement in a closed-loop model built with SC Ventures-backed Zodia Markets.
- The bank called the service a global first for Standard Chartered and plans to expand it to other markets, though it gave no timeline.
Standard Chartered will now let its wealthier clients in the United Arab Emirates buy and sell Bitcoin and Ethereum straight from their bank accounts, the British lender announced Wednesday.
The move eliminates the need for its affluent clients to rely on separate wallets or third-party platforms, the bank said.
The service opens first to clients classified as Professional Investors and runs under licensing approval from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, or VARA. The bank called it a global first for Standard Chartered and the first crypto trading offering from an international bank in the UAE.
Trades are executed inside the bank's own ecosystem, and Standard Chartered handles custody and settlement end-to-end through what it calls a closed-loop model, which the bank says reduces clients' exposure to third-party wallet risk.
The bank built the product across its Wealth and Retail Banking and Corporate and Investment Banking units, working with Zodia Markets, a digital asset trading firm backed by Standard Chartered's venture arm, SC Ventures.
“As client interest in digital assets continues to grow, this launch represents a significant milestone for Standard Chartered as we bring digital assets into our core wealth offering” Samir Subberwal, the bank's global head of wealth solutions, retail products, data and analytics, said. He argued that clients now want more than access, and are looking for the security that comes with buying through a regulated institution.
Rola Abu Manneh, Standard Chartered's CEO for the UAE, Middle East and Pakistan, said the country was a natural choice given its regulatory environment and its role as one of the bank's four global wealth hubs.
Until now, Standard Chartered's crypto trading business had catered to institutions. In July 2025, it became the first global systemically important bank—one of the lenders regulators consider too big to fail—to offer spot trading in Bitcoin and Ethereum to institutional clients, through its U.K. branch.
It brought that institutional desk to the UAE last month through its unit in the Dubai International Financial Centre, which is overseen by a different watchdog, the Dubai Financial Services Authority. The bank's crypto custody service had already gone live in the UAE in September 2024, and in the European Union through a Luxembourg entity a few months later.
Wealth clients previously had indirect routes into crypto at the bank: crypto exchange-traded funds on its cash equities platform, structured products, and over-the-counter derivatives tied to crypto prices. The new service lets them own the coins themselves, held by the bank, rather than a product that tracks their price.
The bank has historically been very bullish towards crypto, with frequent calls from its analysts for Bitcoin to extend to new highs.
In June, Geoff Kendrick, Standard Chartered's global head of digital asset research, declared crypto winter over after Bitcoin slid to nearly $59,000, a 53% drop from its October 2025 peak of $126,000. The bank has held onto a $100,000 year-end target for BTC.

OpenAI eyes security firm purchase amid office bugging scandal
OpenAI is in talks to acquire Trail of Bits (ToB), a cybersecurity firm which counts top crypto projects among its clients, according to a Tuesday report by The Information.
The news comes in the wake of a major security incident at the AI giant’s offices, in which it discovered a “sophisticated recording device” in a conference room, planted by an engineer who’s since been arrested by the FBI.
ToB is one of the best known and well-respected auditors among crypto projects, with experience in nine blockchain ecosystems, and counting Arbitrum, Uniswap and Aave as clients.
Read more: Ledger spyware scare spreads beyond Southeast Asia
OpenAI and ToB previously collaborated on the “Patch the Planet” initiative, part of OpenAI’s wider Daybreak frontier model security program. In 2023, it also audited World (then Worldcoin), with which OpenAI shares a co-founder, Sam Altman.
Earlier this year, ToB produced a set of plug-ins for “security research, vulnerability detection, and audit workflows” via Claude Code, including smart contract vulnerability scanning.
Red teaming
The potential acquisition comes after a major reckoning for top AI companies and the dangers they present.
The discussion kicked off after a rogue swarm of OpenAI agents broke out of their sandbox and attacked the open-source AI platform HuggingFace in July.
While the increasing need for security expertise is clear, both within crypto and the wider AI industry, some find the potential for gatekeeping worrying.
Read more: Claude AI plugins can now vibe code smart contracts
Conversely, Yuga Labs’ 0xQuit called the move “extremely bullish” for crypto security, while another X user suspects OpenAI may be making a move into agentic crypto adoption.
A ToB audit is far from a rubber-stamp for safety, however.
DeFi projects audited by the firm have been exploited in the past, including Balancer and Bunni Finance, which lost $129 million and $8 million, respectively, last year.
Balancer has since decided to shut down.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Turner Wright
items.content:
OCC report finds debanking efforts tied to crypto activities
The report from the US banking regulator did not include specific examples of debanking related to crypto, but mentioned it alongside ties to oil, gas and firearms.
The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) released a report on debanking efforts, including ties to digital assets as activities that influenced banks to limit financial services.
In a report released Wednesday, the OCC said certain banks had “public and nonpublic policies” restricting services for many industries, including oil and gas, tobacco, firearms and digital assets. According to the banking regulator, the report was in accordance with an August 2025 executive order from US President Donald Trump to prevent what he called “unlawful debanking.”
“Many institutions also placed restrictions on banking digital asset activities, including on issuers, exchanges, or administrators, often attributed to financial crime considerations,” said the OCC.
In November 2024, more than 30 tech and crypto executives claimed to have been denied access to banking services. Many in the crypto industry unofficially dubbed the effort as “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” after the Obama-era initiative to fight fraud and money laundering facilitated by banks.
However, Wednesday’s 47-page report did not include specific examples of debanking relating to digital asset activities. The OCC said it had been “unable to quantify on a comprehensive basis the full extent of debanking or alleged debanking actions” based on a review of nine major banks, and the agency’s head, Jonathan Gould, focused largely on the report’s claims around debanking due to ties to coal and firearms.
“These decisions were not based on financial risk,” said Gould, referencing the debanking due to connections to coal. “Instead, banks cited concerns about negative headlines, public protests, and the perceived reputational consequences of supporting the industry.”
The 2025 executive order from Trump followed calls from many in the industry surrounding claims -- including “Operation Chokepoint 2.0” -- that the US government under former President Joe Biden may have influenced financial institutions into cutting off crypto firms from certain services.
Related: Fed seeks feedback on proposal critics say could end Operation Chokepoint 2.0

items.content:
Kalshi CEO says state-led oversight of U.S. prediction markets would push them out
CEO Tarek Mansour said he feels "pretty good" about the pending outcome of the current legal fight over who has the right to regulate prediction markets.
- The CEO of prediction markets firm Kalshi, Tarek Mansour, said that if the U.S. court side with states who claim gambling authorities over such businesses, they’ll be forced offshore.
- Though a couple of federal courts have issued decisions against his view, Mansour suggested he feels “pretty good” about his company’s legal standing in the U.S.
ARLINGTON, Va. — The CEO of Kalshi, the company at the center of a high-profile legal battle over the future of prediction markets in the U.S., said the clash won't ultimately decide whether the rapidly growing industry is overseen by states or a federal agency, but whether it's overseen by the feds here or is forced overseas.
"We feel pretty good about where we stand overall," Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said Wednesday at the DC Fintech Week event near Washington.
Mansour rejected arguments that sports betting — the explosively growing element of the event-contracts space — doesn't have significant economic consequences that justify the trades' status as federally regulated financial contracts.
"The notion that sports does not have economic consequence is ludicrous," he said.
A growing list of states have challenged Kalshi and other prediction markets firms in court, accusing them of engaging in illegal sports wagering that belongs under the authority of state gambling regulators. But Kalshi and the federal regulator of its exchange, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, have countered in courts that the federal agency is the appropriate sole watchdog of prediction markets.
So far, the dispute has risen to a number of federal appellate courts, where the courts have now split, with one major ruling on Kalshi's side and two backing the states' view. As a result, New Jersey asked the U.S. Supreme Court to take the case, and prominent groups have been sharing their views with the high court, including the National Football League.
Mansour said, "It's not a choice of state versus federal market. It's a choice of whether prediction markets exist in the U.S. or whether they go offshore."
He argued that he's considered Kalshi's regulatory relationship since its beginnings, and "it really elegantly fit under definitions of commodity." He said the Commodity Exchange Act was a "truly beautiful statue" that allowed a shift from agricultural futures to oil and metals to less tangible financial products like swaps.
Mansour also responded Wednesday to accusations of inflated trading volume in bitcoin and ether perpetual-futures markets on his platform. He said that "there's a lot of crazy" on social media site X, formerly Twitter. The questions focused on often-recurring trade sizes that represented a significant portion of Kalshi's volume. Mansour pointed again at the Washington event to fixed-size orders from market makers.
"Twitter went, like, 'Oh my God, there's a spike. There must be, you know, like inflation of volume or anything like that.' It's none of it," he said.
"Maybe the broader point about this is how much people misunderstand markets," he said. "They're just complicated. They're not easy to understand."
The CFTC has been making rapid moves to bolster its prediction markets authority. Last week, it issued a rule and proposed another that were meant to place event contracts into the definition of swaps that are explicitly policed by the agency and not by state gambling regulators.

items.author: Cointelegraph by Sam Bourgi
items.content:
Standard Chartered pushes $2T stablecoin forecast to 2030 as transaction volumes grow
The bank identified four distinct stablecoin markets, with USDC leading payments and AI transactions as competition intensifies over reserve yields.
Standard Chartered says stablecoin transaction activity continues to grow even as the market’s overall value has stalled, suggesting existing stablecoins are circulating more frequently rather than new supply driving growth.
In a report shared with Cointelegraph, the bank said it now expects stablecoin market capitalization to reach $2 trillion by 2030, two years later than initially projected, after the market plateaued at roughly $309 billion this year.
Geoffrey Kendrick, StanChart’s head of digital assets research, said stablecoin usage continues to expand despite slower supply growth, with existing stablecoins changing hands more frequently as their use cases diversify.
Kendrick identified four distinct markets, each with different competitive dynamics. Tether’s USDt (USDT) dominates emerging-market savings, while Circle’s USDC (USDC) leads developed-market payments. USDC and Ethena’s USDe have established strong positions in crypto trading, while USDC also leads the much smaller market for transactions between AI agents.
The bank expects the most intense competition in developed market payments, where challengers such as USDG, M^0 and multibank stablecoin networks are pursuing alternatives to existing payment infrastructure.
According to Kendrick, how issuers and payment networks divide the yield generated by stablecoin reserves could ultimately determine which competitors gain market share.
Related: Crypto’s billions are back, but the premiums aren’t
US regulatory and accounting changes could shape stablecoin use
Standard Chartered’s revised forecast comes as regulatory and accounting developments in the United States could influence how businesses use stablecoins.
Since the GENIUS Act passed in 2025, US regulators have proposed rules governing stablecoin issuance, reserve requirements and consumer protections. Some measures have also clarified the limits of those protections, including a Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) proposal that would exclude stablecoin holders from pass-through deposit insurance.
The Treasury Department has also advanced implementation of the law. In August, it proposed rules restricting stablecoin issuance in the United States to federally or state-authorized issuers, with the licensing requirements expected to take effect in January 2027.
Separately, in August, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), which sets US accounting standards, proposed an update that could affect how companies report certain stablecoins on their balance sheets.
Blockchain payments company Tempo said the proposed changes could make it easier for businesses to use stablecoins for payments and settlement without introducing additional accounting complications.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wall Street and crypto fight for the same turf

items.title: Coinbase Warns Bitcoin’s Quantum Security Upgrade Could Take Years

items.author: Decrypt Staff
items.content:
In brief
- Coinbase, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin, urged developers to start preparing for the quantum threat now, warning that consensus changes and migration “can take years.”
- It laid out technical requirements—backing a flexible “container” design like BIP-360, a staged “1-of-2” classical-plus-quantum spending path, and compatibility with the MPC key-splitting custodians rely on.
- The exchange said dormant, lost, and Satoshi-era coins are a separate governance problem.
Coinbase is pressing Bitcoin’s developers to begin preparing for the quantum-computing threat before it’s too late, laying out a detailed technical wish list for how the network should harden itself and arguing the work can’t wait for certainty that a threat has arrived.
In a blog post published Tuesday, the exchange, which says it custodies roughly 5% of all Bitcoin in existence, framed the shift to quantum-resistant cryptography as a complex, multi-year undertaking that needs to start now.
“Bitcoin consensus changes and ecosystem migrations can take years,” the company wrote, warning that waiting for the announcement of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer, the kind capable of breaking Bitcoin’s signatures, would leave too little time to respond.
The concern centers on how Bitcoin secures wallets. A sufficiently powerful quantum machine could, in theory, derive a private key from an exposed public key and drain the funds, a hypothetical milestone the industry calls “Q-Day.”
Coinbase stressed that a fix involves far more than picking a new signature scheme: any transition would need to protect both existing and newly created coins, fit Bitcoin’s limited block space, keep working for ordinary wallets and institutional custody alike, and offer a migration path for coins that never move.
The post reads less like a mandate than a set of requirements from one of the network’s largest stakeholders. Coinbase backed a flexible “container” design, pointing to proposals such as BIP-360, that would let new post-quantum signature systems be swapped in over time without a full redesign.
It also floated a staged “1-of-2” construction, letting the same funds be spent with either a classical key or a quantum-safe one during the transition. The company emphasized that whatever scheme Bitcoin adopts should be compatible with multi-party computation, the key-splitting technique custodians like Coinbase rely on to guard against theft.
Thornier still is the question of dormant, lost, or exposed coins, including Satoshi-era holdings, which Coinbase said should be treated as a separate governance problem. It cautioned that any rescue mechanism must itself be quantum-safe, so an attacker who only knows an exposed public key couldn’t exploit it.
The push builds on Coinbase’s steady drumbeat of quantum warnings.
The exchange convened a quantum advisory board in January o study the risks and develop precisely the sort of guidance it offered this week. The company also joined a Bitcoin Security Consortium in July alongside BlackRock and Strategy, pledging a combined $15 million toward quantum-proofing Bitcoin.

items.content:
Richard Heart arrested in Turkey almost 2 years after Interpol red notice
Richard Heart, the Hex founder wanted by Finland under an Interpol Red Notice, was reportedly arrested by police in Istanbul on Wednesday.
That’s according to Turkish news outlet Haberler, which reports that during the morning raid, police seized $4 million in cash, 64 luxury watches, guns, computers, crypto mining equipment, and other electronic devices from Heart, real name Richard James Schueler.
Euronews reports that three handguns, four rifles, seven magazines, 1,360 rounds of ammunition, and a dagger were also seized.
Read more: Finland wants to detain Richard Heart, alleges millions in unpaid taxes
Istanbul’s National Intelligence Organization (MİT) and local Beşiktaş police conducted the raid, which was coordinated by Istanbul’s Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office, Financial Crimes Divison, Interpol, and MİT.
Haberler reports that the investigation looked into Schueler’s alleged Istanbul-based international fraud network that also held offices across the US, Finland, and Spain.
The price of Schueler’s Hex token plunged almost 45% following the news of his arrest.
US doesn’t want Richard Heart arrested — but Finland does
In 2023, the SEC accused Heart of selling over $1 billion in unregistered securities, and misappropriating millions of dollars from his Hex, PulseChain, and PulseX crypto projects.
He allegedly misused $12 million to purchase sports cars, watches, and a 555-carat black diamond known as “The Enigma.”
Two years later, the lawsuit was dropped after the SEC failed to establish legal jurisdiction. He’s also no longer listed on Europol’s most wanted list, likely due to today’s reported arrest.
Read more: Richard Heart tells court full of US investors that HEX wasn’t aimed at them
An Interpol Red Notice on behalf of Finland was posted in December 2024 for alleged aggravated tax fraud involving hundreds of millions of euros in unpaid tax.
He also allegedly assaulted a minor in 2021.
Heart’s alleged new abode in Istanbul was a luxurious address, potentially paid for using funds linked to suspected crypto mixer transactions through which Heart attempted to obfuscate $500 million worth of crypto.

AI agents make 138 million crypto payments as U.S. dominates spending on AI models
U.S.-linked wallets account for just over 88% of tracked AI model payments, dwarfing China’s 0.1% share, according to new Chainalysis research.
- AI agents made more than 138 million transactions through Coinbase’s x402 protocol, using cryptocurrency to buy data, computing power and access to AI models.
- U.S.-linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of identified payments for AI model inference, while Chinese-linked wallets dominated payments for security and code-analysis services.
- More than 87% of analyzed x402 payments were worth 10 cents or less, underscoring stablecoins’ potential for micropayments while leaving questions about genuine commercial demand.
Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are no longer just talking to each other. They are paying for services, buying data and even purchasing access to tokens the AI models, with more than 138 million transactions recorded through the x402 protocol on Coinbase’s Base blockchain, according to a Chainalysis’ Inside North America's $3 trillion crypto economy: Agentic commerce accelerates report.
The United States dominates this emerging market. U.S.linked wallets accounted for 88.1% of the geographically identified payments for AI model inference, compared with just 0.1% for Chinese-linked wallets, the blockchain analytics firm found.
"One possible explanation is that Chinese developers are more inclined to use open-weight models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, reducing their need to purchase metered inference services," Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' head of research, told CoinDesk.
The findings, released Wednesday, come as Visa, Mastercard, Stripe and other payments giants have backed the x402 protocol, while Coinbase has begun allowing business customers to accept payments from AI agents.
Yat Siu, co-founder and chairman of Animoca Brands, recently told CoinDesk that over the next few years he estimates up to 100 billion AI agents will be transacting on the internet and they will be using crypto. And crypto’s next billion users might be AI agents paying with stablecoins. “Stablecoins are particularly well suited to the kinds of transactions we expect AI agents to make at first,” Stephanie Cohen, Cloudflare’s chief strategy officer, told CoinDesk.
Unlike traditional card payments, stablecoins can handle transactions worth fractions of a cent, allowing AI agents to buy data, computing power and other services without human intervention. The new Chainalysis figures offer evidence of growing use of those payment systems, although transaction counts alone do not establish how much represents genuine commercial demand.
Much of the activity runs through x402, a payments protocol incubated by Coinbase that allows AI agents to pay automatically for digital services using crypto.
More than 87% of x402 payments analyzed by Chainalysis were worth between one-hundredth of a cent and 10 cents, making them too small to process economically through traditional credit card networks.
The amounts remain small. In July, x402 processed roughly 75 million payments worth just $24 million over 30 days. Earlier research also raised questions about artificial activity on the network.
Among wallets first funded in the second quarter of 2026, 89.3% received additional funding within 30 days, compared with 70.6% for wallets first funded in the Q3 2025. The analysis excluded wallets that made payments on one only one day.
The time between a wallet receiving funds and making its first x40 payment also fell sharply, from an average of 73 days in late 2025 to just 18 minutes in Q3 2026.
China, meanwhile, showed a different pattern of activity. Chinese-linked wallets accounted for roughly 90% of geographically identified payments for security and code-analysis services, much of it directed toward AgentLisa, an AI-powered smart contract auditing platform.
He cautioned against interpreting that gap as evidence that open-source AI was undermining Asia's payments market.
"That's one possible interpretation, but we wouldn't go so far as to say open-source AI is starving Asia's on-chain inference market," he said.
The figures measure identifiable transactions through x402, rather than the entire global market for AI payments.
"AI agents are becoming economic actors where every agent is effectively a new 'user' of the blockchain," Tejwani said in the report.
For now, the transactions remain small, but Chainalysis' findings suggest autonomous software is beginning to establish its own spending habits, with the United States leading the market for paid AI services.

StarkWare支持Polymarket用户隐匿下单，新推出OffMarket

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，StarkWare 已向公众开放 OffMarket，用户可在 Polymarket 交易时不把仓位与现有账户公开关联。该服务自 8 月起小范围试用，基于零知识技术与 Starknet 共享隐私资金池，目前每账户存款上限为 1000 枚 USDC，后续将按需求调整；订单仍在 Polymarket 上与同一买卖双方、同一市场价格成交，服务本身非托管，用户密钥留在浏览器端。资金池合约经 OpenZeppelin 审计且未发现严重或高危问题，StarkWare 随后完成形式化验证。

Polymarket 交易记录在 Polygon 上公开，仓位、下单规模与历史均可被查看，OffMarket 仍无法完全避免他人通过成交规模或时机推断交易者身份，市场报价与成交本身仍公开。该产品并非 Polymarket 官方产品、无正式合作或特殊接入权限，属 Polymarket 验证 Builder 计划一部分，并沿用其地理限制包括禁止美国用户。独立合规机构 Financial Privacy Inc. 保管主查看密钥用于制裁筛查及在合法请求下按规定披露信息。

L2BEAT 数据显示，Starknet 该共享隐私池目前约有 150 万美元、1.7 万笔存款。

Crypto Long & Short: Why gold and bitcoin belong in the same portfolio
You're reading Crypto Long & Short, our weekly newsletter featuring insights, news and analysis for the professional investor. Sign up here to get it in your inbox every Wednesday.
Note: The views expressed in this column are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect those of CoinDesk, Inc., CoinDesk Indices or its owners and affiliates.
Happy Wednesday,
This is your institutional newsletter, Crypto Long & Short. This week:
- Steve Neamtz of Yorkville America on what gold has that bitcoin is still building
- Top headlines institutions should pay attention to by Francisco Rodrigues
- “CHIP rebounds as USD.AI pivots to a loan factory” in Chart of the Week
…and if you’re looking for bitcoin meets Broadway: Crypto is taking the stage in New York City. “Bitcoin Bad Boy,” a comedy by Ben Schiller, runs Oct. 15-25 at the Chain Theatre. The show centers around a family in debt, a coder who wants to build a better world and a memecoin. Learn more.
Thanks for joining us!
Gold and bitcoin are allies against debasement
by Steve Neamtz, CEO, Yorkville America
Gold trading near $4,200 an ounce alongside bitcoin 
For 5,000 years, gold has demonstrated its value as a reserve asset. Bitcoin’s 17-year history offers far less empirical evidence. But the supply of both assets cannot be expanded by central bank or fiscal policymakers. Their shared scarcity thus takes on greater significance in a world awash in debt.
In the United States alone, the federal debt has climbed past $39 trillion. The U.S. now spends roughly $1 trillion a year simply servicing its existing debt, and the outlook is even more challenging for much of the developed world. Currencies often serve as the relief valve for fiscal concerns. The U.S. dollar, for example, has lost roughly 40% of its purchasing power over the past two decades.
Against this backdrop, it is important to understand where we believe supply-constrained assets fit within long-term diversified portfolios. A 2025 study in Resources Policy, using multifractal cross-correlation analysis across six asset classes — developed and emerging equities, bonds, commodities, energy and crypto — found that “neither gold nor bitcoin can be classified as a hedge or safe haven for financial markets” under rigorous testing.
That’s a finding about market-drawdown behavior — whether either asset reliably moves against stocks and bonds when markets fall. It says nothing about whether either holds value relative to a currency that is slowly, but steadily, depreciating against them. Investors and allocators buying gold or bitcoin often aren’t using them as shock absorbers. They’re making a debasement bet: that an asset independent of any government’s promise to pay provides diversification benefits.
On that bet, gold and bitcoin aren’t racing against each other — they’re at different points on the same course. Gold already has the custody, legal and reserve-eligibility infrastructure that lets central banks act on a debasement and reserve-currency diversification thesis today. Bitcoin doesn’t yet — at least not fully.
Gold’s lead reflects decades of built plumbing, not a stronger claim to the thesis. Bitcoin does not have the same penetration in terms of knowledge. It is earlier on the same curve, not a different one, and it often appeals to a younger generation of investors.
Central banks bought a record 289 metric tons of gold in the second quarter of 2026, after 244 metric tons in the first, according to data from an industry body funded by mining interests. This is worth flagging even as the pace of buying is independently corroborated elsewhere, and the clearest signal of where reserve managers are putting money and why. Bitcoin is being bought into the same thesis through a newer wrapper: spot ETFs, which solve the custody problem but not the sovereign-reserve status central banks need.
None of this requires picking a side. Central banks are buying gold on infrastructure that already exists; institutions are buying bitcoin on infrastructure still being built — the same debasement logic, two different stages. Financial media has already started calling it one trade, not two competing ones, as coverage of the “debasement trade” picked up through 2026. The right question for 2027 isn’t which asset wins. It’s how much of each diversifier belongs in a portfolio built for eroding purchasing power. The volatility is very different between gold and bitcoin, and we believe solutions that help investors with sizing these two anti-debasement assets will add value to portfolio construction efforts.
Headlines of the week
This week’s headlines show institutional crypto expanding through bank trading, regulated custody and national ETF access, while European regulators moved to force unauthorized stablecoins off trading platforms.
- EU gives crypto platforms three months to remove unauthorized stablecoins: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) told authorized platforms to block new trading and purchases of stablecoins that do not comply with the Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation (MiCA), with national regulators expected to resolve existing customer holdings within three months.
- Russia’s largest bank secures approval to trade crypto: Sberbank joined the country’s crypto exchange register and plans to open trading to all clients on Dec. 1, with bitcoin, ether and tether already being tested in its app.
- Ledger says spy chip in resold devices stole wallet recovery phrases: A covert implant in signers sold by reseller CryptoBilis read recovery phrases from device screens and sent them over a mobile network, with onchain researchers estimating up to $93.2 million lost across more than 300 wallets.
- Thailand opens its stock exchange to locally listed bitcoin and ether ETFs: Rules taking effect Oct. 16 will let domestic asset managers launch single-asset crypto funds, provided at least 80% of their net assets track bitcoin or ether and regulated custodians hold the tokens.
- Standard Chartered launches institutional RLUSD custody in Dubai: The bank now holds Ripple’s stablecoin for eligible clients and plans to connect those holdings to LMAX so they can serve as trading collateral without leaving the bank, subject to approvals and testing.
Chart of the week
CHIP rebounds as USD.AI pivots to a loan factory
USD.AI active loans dropped ~22% to ~$311 million on Oct. 2 and have been flat since, while CHIP has rebounded ~35% since Oct. 1 to ~5.8 cents (still ~48% below its April high). The catalyst is GLX, a loan-factory model (originate, sell performing loans to institutions, recycle the capital), which could drive a rebound in active loans by recycling capital into new loans without a much bigger balance sheet.

Former FTX Europe Head’s Perpetuals com Files to Trade Tokenized U.S. Stocks Under SEC Innovation Exemption

Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals com, led by former FTX Europe head Patrick Gruhn, has filed with the SEC to operate a tokenized securities venue under the five-year Innovation Exemption.

It is the second firm to pursue U.S. tokenized stock trading under the framework, after the OKX-ICE joint venture. Tokens must carry the same dividend and voting rights as ordinary shares, and companies have 30 days to object.

Trading is planned via permissioned AMM pools on its Ethereum-compatible L2 Kronos X Public, with USDC as the settlement asset. A launch could come as early as mid-November. — link

items.author: Jose Antonio Lanz
items.content:
In brief
- U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year in September, above the 3.6% forecast, as gasoline jumped 9.1% in a single month.
- Odds of an October Fed rate hike roughly doubled from 22% after the report, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.3%.
- Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $82,142 and is holding the $81,847 to $82,305 Fibonacci golden zone, with $81,603 as the next support.
Bitcoin fell 1.5% to $82,142 on Wednesday after U.S. inflation came in hotter than expected, dragging most of the crypto market down with it. Ethereum dropped 2.8% to $2,440, Solana lost 1.9% and XRP slid 1.3%, while total crypto market cap shed 0.7% to $2.8 trillion.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.6% in September and 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Economists expected 3.6%. Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in a single month and accounted for more than half of the increase.
Core CPI, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 2.6% annually against a 2.5% forecast. That is the reading the Federal Reserve watches most closely, since it shows whether price pressure is spreading into rent, airfares, and services.
Expensive gasoline starts with expensive oil, which has traded above $90 a barrel for most of the past two months amid the war between the U.S. and Iran. Pricier fuel raises the cost of shipping and producing almost everything.
When inflation runs hot, the Fed raises interest rates to cool spending. It already hiked in September to a 3.75%-4.00% range, and traders now see roughly 44% to 49% odds of another hike at its October 27-28 meeting, up from 22% before the report, according to CME FedWatch.
The 2-year Treasury yield, which closely tracks Fed rate expectations, jumped about 10 basis points to roughly 4.9%, while the 10-year climbed to about 5.3%, near 24-year highs.
Higher yields hit crypto directly. A government bond paying 5.3% with almost no risk competes with Bitcoin, which pays nothing. Rising rates also make borrowing more expensive and tend to strengthen the dollar, draining the cheap money speculative assets feed on, which is why the S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq 0.8% on the same news.
Crypto also swings harder than stocks because many traders borrow to bet on rising prices, and when the price drops past a set level, exchanges automatically close those positions, a process called liquidation, and that forced selling can push prices lower and trigger more liquidations in a chain.
At the moment, more than $281 million in crypto derivatives positions have been liquidated in the past 24 hours, with most of it coming in just the last four hours—and the majority of that coming from Bitcoin long positions (the bulls betting the price would go up, and now paying the price when it dropped).
Bitcoin price: The macro picture is punching hard
On the daily chart, Bitcoin opened at $83,066 and now trades near $82,211, sitting inside the Fibonacci "golden zone" it reclaimed on Tuesday. That zone marks an area where pullbacks within uptrends often attract buyers.
The average price of the last 50 days remains above the 200-day average, a setup traders read as an intact long-term uptrend. The Average Directional Index, which gauges trend strength on a 0-to-100 scale where readings above 25 confirm a trend, sits at 27.7 with buyers still ahead, down from 29.9 on Tuesday, meaning traders are bullish, just not as much as they used to be.
The Relative Strength Index, a momentum gauge from 0 to 100, slipped to 48.7, just under the 50 line that separates bullish from bearish momentum. The Squeeze Momentum Indicator has been on for eight sessions, meaning volatility is compressed and a big move is building, and its -0.76 reading leans bearish by a small margin.
A daily close below $81,603 would break the golden zone and bring the $80,365 swing low into play, with the trend band near $80,284 right under it; losing that would expose $78,003. On the upside, bulls need to reclaim $84,245 before targeting $85,301, $86,644 and the October high of $87,422.
The next test arrives Thursday with the Producer Price Index, which tracks what businesses pay for goods and services, and the Fed announces its rate decision on October 28.

items.content:
Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflation
Bitcoin fell below $82,000 while bond yields targeted new 24-year highs on the back of hot US CPI inflation.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $82,000 after Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US consumer inflation beat expectations.
Key points:
- Bitcoin dropped to $81,926 on Bitstamp after US September CPI inflation came in at 3.7% versus expectations of 3.6%.
- Fuel-price increases accounted for the lion’s share of the gain at 9.1% year-on-year.
- US bond yields spiked on the news, while gold fell to $4,079 per ounce.
Bitcoin slips under $82,000 on higher US CPI print
Data from TradingView showed crypto, gold and stock-market futures dropping after the release of Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At 3.7% year-on-year, this came in 0.1% above majority market consensus, data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) confirmed. The increase in fuel prices around the Middle East conflict and oil-supply crisis was conspicuous.
“The index for gasoline rose 9.1 percent in September, accounting for over half of the monthly all items increase. The energy index increased 5.2 percent over the month following a 2.1-percent increase in August,” an official release stated.
US CPI 12-month % change. Source: BLS
Inflation nonetheless increased across the board, as core CPI — the index minus energy and food — also came in 0.1% higher than anticipated at 2.6% year-on-year.
Commenting, Sonu Varghese, chief macro strategist at Carson Group, suggested that elevated figures should be a foregone conclusion.
“The only surprise is that investors keep getting surprised by broad-based inflation. And we’ve yet to see the full impact of higher diesel prices and the AI boom,” he told CNBC.
The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed markets adjusting expectations of Federal Reserve policy as a result of the data. The majority now favored a 25-basis-point interest-rate hike at the Fed’s upcoming meeting on Oct. 28, with the odds of that outcome at 53.7% versus 22.1% the day prior. For December, meanwhile, the odds of a second 25-basis-point hike stood at 50%.
Fed target-rate probabilities for October FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
“Taken in combination with the soft payroll numbers in the September employment report, the FOMC is probably on hold for any rate moves at the upcoming October 27-28 meeting although with a definite bias toward a hike in December,” said Theresa Sheehan, economic analyst at Econoday.
As Cointelegraph reported, the next key US inflation data release, the September print of the Producer Price Index (PPI), is due on Friday.
Analysis: High CPI “last thing global bond markets needed”
Gold fell as low as $4,079 per ounce on the back of the CPI result, while US bond yields spiked.
Related: CryptoQuant’s 3 charts keeping Bitcoin’s ‘Uptober’ thesis valid
The 10-year yield, highly sensitive to energy-price triggers, hit 5.329%, around three basis points off new 24-year highs.
“This is the last thing global bond markets needed. Prior to this number, it looked like the global bond sell-off was calming, but now bond markets are catching on fire again,” economist Robin Brooks wrote in a blog post.
US 10-year bond yield one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
BTC price action continued to circle a key area between $82,500 and $83,400, with analysis still waiting for the market to make a decision on its status as support.
items.title: Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflation

Perpetuals com拟借SEC「创新豁免」推出美股代币化交易

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，美股上市金融科技公司 Perpetuals com（代码 PDC）提交通知，计划在美国 SEC 为期五年的「创新豁免」框架下运营代币化证券交易场所，由特拉华州子公司 Kephas Corporation 运营。交易将通过许可制自动做市商（AMM）流动性池进行，初期部署在该公司开发的以太坊兼容 Layer 2 链 Kronos X Public 上，代币化美股将与稳定币 USDC 配对。按通知后 30 天要求，交易最早可能于 11 月中旬启动，尚需完成合规、行情数据与智能合约安全等准备。

「创新豁免」允许特定场所在公链上交易美股而无需注册为传统证券交易平台，代币须具备与普通股票同等的股东权利，包含含分红与投票权，相关上市公司可在 30 天内提出异议。Perpetuals com 由此成为继 OKXICE 之后，第二家按该框架推进代币化美股市场的公司。

其首席执行官 Patrick Gruhn 曾联合创立瑞士代币化公司 Digital Assets AG，协助交易平台推出与特斯拉、Coinbase 等股票挂钩的代币，后被 FTX 收购，Gruhn 曾负责 FTX Europe。

items.content:
In brief
- Turkish police and intelligence officers detained Hex founder Richard Heart in Istanbul on Wednesday, Turkish media reported, acting on an Interpol Red Notice.
- Finland sought the notice in 2024 on a charge of aggravated tax fraud, and Heart was detained along with his wife, according to the reports.
- The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission accused Heart in 2023 of raising more than $1 billion in unregistered crypto offerings, but later dropped the case.
Turkish authorities have detained Richard Heart, the founder of the Hex cryptocurrency, in Istanbul on an Interpol Red Notice, Daily Sabah reported on Wednesday, citing Turkish news agency IHA.
Heart, whose legal name is Richard James Schueler, was detained with his wife on Wednesday morning in an operation by Istanbul police and Turkey's National Intelligence Organization (MIT), according to the report. Police had monitored his address in the city's Beşiktaş district before the arrest.
Officers seized a dozen mobile phones, several laptops, graphics cards, rifles, pistols, two drones, gold bracelets and a large amount of cash in different currencies, IHA reported.
A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition or similar legal action, and is not an international arrest warrant. Interpol issued the notice for Heart in 2024 at the request of Finland. The notice lists a single charge, aggravated tax fraud, though Finnish authorities have also sought him over an alleged assault. Daily Sabah described the notice as relating to high-value cryptocurrency fraud.
Heart and Hex
Heart launched Hex in 2018, marketing it as a high-yield "blockchain certificate of deposit."
In 2023, the SEC charged Heart and three entities he controlled, Hex, PulseChain and PulseX, with conducting unregistered offerings of crypto asset securities that raised more than $1 billion. It also accused him of misappropriating at least $12 million of investor funds to buy luxury goods, including sports cars, watches and a 555-carat black diamond known as "The Enigma."
A federal judge dismissed the complaint in February 2025 for lack of jurisdiction, finding that Heart's activities were not clearly aimed at U.S. investors. The SEC declined to amend it by an April deadline, ending the case, which Heart's lawyer called "a complete victory."
It was not immediately clear whether Finnish authorities have requested Heart's extradition from Turkey.

「美联储传声筒」：通胀高于预期，进一步支持美联储年内再加息

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 14 日，有「美联储传声筒」之称的《华尔街日报》记者 Nick Timiraos 表示，9 月潜在通胀连续第二个月高于预期，进一步强化了美联储年内再次加息的理由。上个月美联储官员一致投票决定加息，几乎所有官员当时都预计年内还将再加息一次。剔除食品和能源价格后的核心 CPI9 月环比上涨 0.33%，高于华尔街经济学家的几乎所有预测。8 月核心 CPI 环比上涨 0.29%。这份报告给美联储官员带来了两个问题。更紧迫的问题是，在官员近期表示预计不会在两周后的会议上调整利率后，他们是否还能等到 12 月再度加息。

一些分析人士认为，如果官员预计最终要加息，就没有太多理由继续等待，尽管美联储官员尚未表现出仅凭一份报告就重新考虑政策安排的迹象。更重要的问题是，利率最终需要升至多高的水平。这取决于能源价格上涨和人工智能投资热潮带来的压力，是否会进一步蔓延至整体经济。

items.content:
In brief
- Ledger has asked resellers and distributors in six Southeast Asian countries and Hong Kong to suspend sales of its devices while it investigates tampered wallets.
- The company said the only confirmed incidents remain in Southeast Asia, and that it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere.
- MediaMarkt Saturn has stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online after a customer in Germany reported an implant, though no funds were lost.
Ledger has asked resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to stop selling its hardware wallets and take them off the shelves while it investigates devices fitted with a hidden implant, the company said in a tweet on Tuesday.
The request covers Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong.
Incident Update - Oct 13th, 2026
Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to suspend sales of Ledger devices while the investigation is ongoing. This includes taking products off the shelves.
Specifically the countries are: Indonesia,…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 13, 2026
The only confirmed incidents remain in Southeast Asia, Ledger said, and it has not verified a drain linked to a device bought elsewhere. The company has previously said that all confirmed losses involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, a reseller in the region.
Ledger is still working to establish who tampered with the devices and at what point in the distribution chain. It said it has no indication that its own infrastructure, systems, services or direct sales channel have been compromised.
Ledger's Donjon security team found that the implant reads the 24-word recovery phrase from the device's screen during setup and sends it out over LTE. Anyone holding that phrase can restore the wallet and move its funds. Onchain investigator Specter has traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts, a figure Ledger says it has not verified.
Earlier on Tuesday, MediaMarkt Saturn stopped selling Ledger devices in its stores and online, with Ledger's agreement, after a customer in Germany reported an implant, Ledger said in a separate tweet. No loss of funds was reported.
Rival hardware wallet maker Trezor said on Tuesday that it will end its authorizations for resellers on January 1, 2027, describing the move as a "precautionary measure." Trezor said there was no evidence that its own devices had been compromised.

items.author: Ryan Gladwin
items.content:
In brief
- Floyd Mayweather's social media accounts promoted a Solana-based meme coin on Monday, which peaked at a $1 million market cap before plummeting in value.
- Notorious celebrity coin promoter Sahil Arora is claiming responsibility for the token and says it's the start of another wave coming to the blockchain.
- Arora has faced accusations of "scamming" celebrities and "rug pulling" tokens, since he exploded onto the scene in 2024 by creating a Caitlyn Jenner meme coin.
Sahil Arora, the notorious promoter behind a string of 2024 celebrity meme coins, just launched a new one, with Floyd Mayweather’s social media accounts briefly promoting it. Arora told Decrypt it’s the start of a comeback: he wants to revive the celebrity coin craze on Solana trading platform Fomo, the same trick that made his name on Pump.fun.
Arora made his name through a series of celebrity-linked meme coin launches on Pump.fun in 2024. It started with former Olympian Caitlyn Jenner, who went on to claim that Arora "scammed" her. Since then, he has been tied to several other projects that celebrities and industry experts have labelled as "rug pulls" or simply fraudulent.
His latest entry is the Floyd Money Mayweather meme coin launched on Fomo, which peaked at just a $1 million market cap before plummeting 96% over the next three hours on Wednesday.
Mayweather's social media account promoted the token, according to several social media accounts, before selling from the deployer wallet for just $5,000 worth of profit and deleting the posts. The token then pumped to its $1 million market cap peak, which meant the wallet lost out on major profits—but Arora says this was all part of the plan.
The coin promoter told Decrypt that the entire scheme was orchestrated, explaining that the narrative of Mayweather fumbling gains was what pushed the token's price higher. Fomo is a trading platform that blends social media elements, meaning that you can see who is buying and selling—which can create viral moments.
Arora claims to have profited seven-figures on the Mayweather token by selling from other wallets. However, on-chain analytics firm Bubblemaps doesn't think that is realistic. The biggest connected cluster of wallets profited approximately $105,000, Bubblemaps told Decrypt, and the top 100 traders combined only made $306,000 worth of profit. So, the analytics firm said numbers aren't adding up.
Still, it appears that the crypto coin promoter stood to profit handsomely from the scheme and is plotting to do it again.
JUST IN: FLOYD MAYWEATHER CREATES A FOMO ACCOUNT AND SHILLS A MEMECOIN
HE SOLD FOR $5,000 PROFIT BEFORE THE COIN RAN, MISSING OUT ON OVER $280,000 IN PROFIT pic.twitter.com/UAX2KWpo5x
— Market Insider (@MrketInsider) October 13, 2026
"We will recreate everything on Fomo that we made on Pump.fun in 2024, just with better strategies where people also win," Arora told Decrypt. When pushed on the new strategies, he said, "this wasn’t [sold in] one clip," in contrast to previous projects that have faced "rug pull" accusations after dropping more than 90% in seconds.
He added that he is "tight" with all of the celebrities that he launches tokens with, and convincing them to be part of his schemes is "really easy."
In 2024, Pump.fun provided Arora with a platform to easily create tokens for celebrities to promote via social media chatter. Now, Fomo has created a trading environment that drives virality, and Arora wants to take advantage of that.
This isn’t Mayweather’s first crypto rodeo. In 2017, he asked fans to start calling him Floyd 'Crypto' Mayweather, dropping his usual 'money' moniker, as he started to plug a streak of token sales.
One of those sales was the Centra Tech initial coin offering, or ICO, which raised $32 million for a crypto debit card it told investors was backed by Visa and Mastercard—it wasn't. By 2018, he was charged by the SEC for promoting the sale without disclosing that he'd been paid. He later agreed to pay a fine and not promote any security for three years.
But in 2021, he gained even more heat for his promotion of an obscure Ethereum-based token named EthereumMax. The boxer turned up to a Bitcoin conference wearing an EthereumMax and was booed by the crowd for suggesting other tokens could succeed in front of a crowd of Bitcoin maximalists. Mayweather was named alongside Kim Kardashian in a lawsuit regarding EthereumMax, though the judge dismissed it by the end of 2022.
This Arora-linked token is just the latest chapter in Mayweather’s long, messy history with crypto.
Floyd Mayweather did not respond to Decrypt's request for comment.
